definition_zh: 结冰；冻结；冰点以下的；极冷的；冷冻保存
definition_en: the process of turning into ice, or weather cold enough to freeze water
core_image: 清晨的水洼表面结成一层硬冰，下面的水还在，冰面却已能承住脚
scene: 清晨池塘边缘的水正在结冰。 The pond was freezing at the edges by early morning.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「水正在变成冰的过程」（第 1 个义项：结冰过程）；句意为清晨池塘边缘正在结冰。

pos.zh: freeze 的现在分词，表示正在冻结

senses.title: Water turning to ice
senses.definition: the process by which liquid water becomes solid ice
senses.definitionCN: 液态水变成固态冰的过程
senses.example: The pond was freezing at the edges by early morning.
senses.exampleCN: 清晨池塘边缘正在结冰。
senses.why: The -ing form names an ongoing change of state, not the finished ice.
senses.whyCN: -ing 形式命名一个正在进行的状态变化，而不是已经完成的冰。

senses.title: Weather below zero
senses.definition: extremely cold weather, at or below the freezing point
senses.definitionCN: 处于或低于冰点的极冷天气
senses.example: Freezing weather kept the harbour closed for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 冰点以下的天气使港口关闭了一周。
senses.why: As an adjective the word describes air that would freeze water, so it works as a weather label.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，它描述能把水冻住的空气，因此可用作天气标签。

senses.title: The freezing point
senses.definition: the temperature at which a liquid becomes solid
senses.definitionCN: 液体变成固体的温度
senses.example: Salt lowers the freezing point of water below zero.
senses.exampleCN: 盐把水的冰点降到零下。
senses.why: The process named by the participle supplies the fixed phrase for its threshold temperature.
senses.whyCN: 分词所命名的过程，为其临界温度提供了固定短语。

senses.title: Preserving food by cold
senses.definition: storing food at temperatures low enough to stop spoilage
senses.definitionCN: 在低到足以阻止腐败的温度下储存食物
senses.example: Freezing keeps the berries firm for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 冷冻能让浆果紧实保存一年。
senses.why: Industry turned the physical process into a storage method and kept the participle as its name.
senses.whyCN: 工业把这个物理过程变成储存方法，并保留了分词作为名称。

senses.title: An official freeze
senses.definition: a government or company order that wages, prices or funds may not change
senses.definitionCN: 政府或公司规定工资、价格或资金不得变动的命令
senses.example: The freezing of rents lasted through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 租金冻结持续了整个冬天。
senses.why: Money that cannot move is imagined as water that cannot flow, so the cold image becomes economic policy.
senses.whyCN: 不能流动的钱被想象成不能流动的水，于是寒冷的意象变成了经济政策。

senses.title: Frosty nights
senses.definition: nights cold enough to leave frost on the ground
senses.definitionCN: 冷到能在地面留下霜的夜晚
senses.example: Freezing nights have already hardened the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 寒冷的夜晚已经把土壤冻硬了。
senses.why: The adjective extends from the temperature to the kind of night that produces visible frost.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从温度延伸到会产生可见白霜的那种夜晚。

senses.title: Cold treatment in medicine
senses.definition: the use of extreme cold to destroy or remove tissue
senses.definitionCN: 用极低温破坏或去除组织的做法
senses.example: Freezing removes the wart without cutting.
senses.exampleCN: 冷冻法不用刀就能去除疣。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the process as a tool, naming the treatment after the cold itself.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这个过程当作工具，用寒冷本身来命名治疗。

senses.title: Freeze-thaw weathering
senses.definition: the repeated freezing and thawing of water in rock cracks
senses.definitionCN: 岩石裂缝中的水反复冻结与融化
senses.example: Freezing splits the limestone a little more each winter.
senses.exampleCN: 每个冬天，冻结都让石灰岩多裂开一点。
senses.why: Water expands as it freezes, so the participle names the geological force that pries rock apart.
senses.whyCN: 水结冰时膨胀，于是这个分词命名了把岩石撬开的地质力量。

intro.en: Freezing is the participle of freeze plus -ing. The verb is native Germanic; its PIE root is a reconstruction. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: freezing 是 freeze 加分词后缀 -ing。动词是日耳曼本土词；其原始印欧语词根属重构形式。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Freeze goes back to Old English freosan, a strong verb with past tense freas and participle froren.
items.cn: freeze 源自古英语 freosan，是一个强变化动词，过去式为 freas，过去分词为 froren。

items.en: The verb is reconstructed as *freusan, with German frieren and Dutch vriezen as close relatives.
items.cn: 该动词被重构为 *freusan，德语 frieren 与荷兰语 vriezen 是近亲。

items.en: The standard reconstruction is PIE *preus- 'to freeze, burn with cold', also behind Latin pruina 'hoarfrost'.
items.cn: 标准重构为原始印欧语 *preus-「冻结、冻得发疼」，拉丁语 pruina「白霜」也出自此。

items.en: Middle English replaced the old participle with frozen, modelled on the past participle of strong verbs, and the -ing form became the regular participle.
items.cn: 中古英语以 frozen 取代旧分词，仿照强变化动词的过去分词形式，-ing 形式则成为规则分词。

items.en: Freezing point is fixed as a scientific phrase in the eighteenth century, and industrial food freezing develops in the nineteenth.
items.cn: freezing point 在十八世纪被固定为科学短语，工业食品冷冻在十九世纪发展起来。

items.en: The economic 'freeze' and the medical cold treatment both standardize the participle as a technical noun.
items.cn: 经济上的「冻结」与医学冷冻治疗都把这一分词固定为技术名词。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to freezing; group two holds adjectives for extreme cold.
note.cn: 第一组是与 freezing 字形或读音接近的词；第二组是表示极冷的形容词。

entries.definition: A decorative band along a wall, or a heavy woollen cloth; it is a noun with no idea of ice.
entries.definitionCN: 墙面上的装饰带，或厚重毛呢；它是名词，与冰无关。

entries.definition: Something given for free; it comes from free, not from freeze.
entries.definitionCN: 免费赠品；出自 free，而不是 freeze。

entries.definition: The act of expelling air suddenly through the nose; only the -ing ending matches.
entries.definitionCN: 突然从鼻子喷气的动作；只有 -ing 词尾相同。

entries.definition: Already turned to ice; it is the result, while freezing is the process.
entries.definitionCN: 已经变成冰；它是结果，而 freezing 是过程。

entries.definition: Covered with ice or very cold in manner; it describes a surface or a tone, not a process.
entries.definitionCN: 覆着冰的，或态度冰冷的；它描述表面或语气，而不是过程。

entries.definition: Extremely cold, often in a formal or technical tone; it comes from Latin frigidus, a different family.
entries.definitionCN: 极冷的，常带正式或技术语气；出自拉丁语 frigidus，属另一词族。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real verb forms, real compounds, and one genuine Latin cognate.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的动词形式、真实的复合词，以及一个真正的拉丁同源词。

normal.en: freeze–froze–frozen: the old strong verb keeps its irregular past, and freezing is the regular -ing form built on the base.
normal.cn: freeze–froze–frozen：这个古老强变化动词保留不规则过去式，freezing 则是在词基上加规则 -ing。

normal.en: freezer = freeze + -er, the appliance that does the freezing.
normal.cn: freezer = freeze + -er，做冷冻这件事的器具。

normal.en: freezing point pairs the process with its threshold, just as boiling point does for heat.
normal.cn: freezing point 把过程与临界点配对，正如 boiling point 对热所做的那样。

normal.en: freeze-dry = freeze + dry: ice is removed as vapour without melting, a real preservation method.
normal.cn: freeze-dry = freeze + dry：冰不经融化直接升华，是真实的保存方法。

normal.en: anti-freeze = anti- (against) + freeze, the additive that stops a radiator from freezing.
normal.cn: anti-freeze = anti-「反对」+ freeze，防止水箱结冰的添加剂。

abstract.en: Abstractly, freezing is motion stopping: water loses its flow and becomes a solid that holds its shape.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，freezing 是运动停止：水失去流动，变成保持形状的固体。

abstract.en: The same stopping can be applied to wages, to tissue, to a pond or to a rock crack.
abstract.cn: 同样的「停住」可以用在工资、组织、池塘或岩石裂缝上。

abstract.en: So freezing is not simply cold but the moment a thing can no longer move.
abstract.cn: 所以 freezing 不只是冷，而是一物再也不能移动的那一刻。

examples.en: Freezing temperatures overnight damaged the young shoots.
examples.cn: 夜间的零下气温冻坏了新芽。

examples.en: The lab stores the samples by freezing them in liquid nitrogen.
examples.cn: 实验室用液氮冷冻保存样本。

examples.en: Freezing and thawing slowly breaks the cliff face apart.
examples.cn: 冻融交替慢慢把崖面裂开。

dict_mnemonic.text: freeze（冻住）+ -ing：正在冻住 → freezing 结冰、极冷的

root: freeze 源自古英语 freosan，出自原始日耳曼语 *freusan，更早重构为原始印欧语 *preus-「冻结」；freezing 为其 -ing 分词形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow water losing its motion: the process, the cold air, the threshold, food storage, a price freeze, frosty nights, cold surgery and the freeze-thaw that splits rock.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着「水失去运动」展开：过程、冷空气、临界点、食物储存、价格冻结、有霜的夜、冷冻手术，以及把岩石劈开的冻融。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: liquid stops moving and locks into a shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：液体停止流动，锁定成一个形状。

branches.en: PHYSICAL PROCESS: a pond and a rock crack freeze by the same expansion of water.
branches.cn: 物理过程：池塘与岩石裂缝靠同一个水膨胀原理冻结。

branches.en: WEATHER: air below zero and the frosty night it produces.
branches.cn: 天气：零下的空气与它带来的霜夜。

branches.en: THRESHOLD: the process becomes a fixed number on a thermometer.
branches.cn: 临界点：过程变成温度计上的一个固定数字。

branches.en: METHOD: industry uses the process to keep food from spoiling.
branches.cn: 方法：工业用这个过程防止食物腐败。

branches.en: STOPPING THINGS: money and tissue are both held still by cold or by order.
branches.cn: 使物停住：资金与组织都被寒冷或命令定住。

intro.en: Freezing belongs to the freeze family: -er names the machine, -ing names the process, and compounds like anti-freeze and freeze-dry add direction or method.
intro.cn: freezing 属于 freeze 词族：-er 命名机器，-ing 命名过程，anti-freeze、freeze-dry 等复合词则补充方向或方法。

latinIntro.en: Freeze is Germanic, but it shares a PIE root with Latin pruina 'hoarfrost'. The Latin entries below are cognates, not ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: freeze 属日耳曼语，但与拉丁语 pruina「白霜」共享原始印欧语词根。下面的拉丁条目是同源词，不是祖先。

items.meaning: to turn to ice; also a government order stopping prices
items.meaningCN: 结冰；也指政府停止价格变动的命令
items.example: The lake freezes in December.

items.meaning: an appliance that keeps things frozen
items.meaningCN: 使物品保持冷冻的器具（-er 表示施动者或工具）
items.example: Put the meat in the freezer.

items.structure: old strong past participle of freeze
items.meaning: turned to ice; also unable to move
items.meaningCN: 已冻成冰的；也指动弹不得的
items.example: The pipes were frozen solid.

items.meaning: the temperature at which a liquid solidifies
items.meaningCN: 液体凝固的温度，即冰点
items.example: Brine has a lower freezing point than water.

items.meaning: to preserve by freezing and then removing ice as vapour
items.meaningCN: 先冷冻再让冰直接升华的干燥保存法
items.example: They freeze-dry the coffee for instant use.
items.exampleCN: 他们把咖啡冻干做成速溶。

items.meaning: a liquid added to water to stop it freezing
items.meaningCN: 加入水中防止结冰的液体（anti- 表示「抗、防」）
items.example: Check the anti-freeze before winter.

items.meaning: a very cold freezer, or to store at very low temperature
items.meaningCN: 深度冷冻柜；或指在极低温下储存
items.example: The specimens went into deep-freeze.

items.meaning: rain that stays liquid in cold air and freezes on contact
items.meaningCN: 在冷空气中保持液态、触物即冻的雨，即冻雨
items.example: Freezing rain closed the airport.

definition_zh: 甲壳动物（虾、蟹、藤壶等有硬壳的节肢动物）
definition_en: an arthropod with a hard shell, such as a crab, shrimp, lobster or barnacle
core_image: 潮池石缝里一只螃蟹举起硬壳钳子，壳面反着水光
scene: 潮池里，一只小蟹横着快跑，硬壳在浅水中反着光。 A small crustacean scuttled sideways through the pool, its hard shell glinting under the water.
sceneCN: 这里 crustacean 指「甲壳动物」（第 1 个义项：有硬壳的节肢动物）；句意为一只小甲壳动物横着穿过潮池，硬壳在水下反光。

derivatives.zh: 十足目动物（蟹、虾等甲壳动物）

senses.title: A member of the group Crustacea
senses.definition: any arthropod of the group Crustacea, with a hard exoskeleton and usually two pairs of antennae
senses.definitionCN: 甲壳动物类群中任何有硬外骨骼、通常有两对触角的节肢动物
senses.example: A small crustacean scuttled sideways through the pool.
senses.exampleCN: 一只小甲壳动物横着穿过潮池。
senses.why: The name comes from Latin crusta 'shell', because the group is defined by its hard casing.
senses.whyCN: 名字来自拉丁 crusta「硬壳」，因为这一类群正是以硬壳为标志。

senses.title: The group as a whole
senses.definition: the crustaceans collectively, treated as one large subgroup of arthropods
senses.definitionCN: 把所有甲壳动物作为一个大的节肢动物亚群来看
senses.example: Crustaceans dominate the tide pool at night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里潮池由甲壳类占据主导。
senses.why: Collective use lets the plural stand for the group without naming each species.
senses.whyCN: 集合用法让复数形式代表整个类群，无需逐一命名物种。

senses.title: An edible crustacean
senses.definition: a crab, shrimp, lobster or similar animal harvested for food
senses.definitionCN: 作为食物捕捞的蟹、虾、龙虾或类似动物
senses.example: The restaurant buys crustaceans from the local boats.
senses.exampleCN: 这家餐厅从本地渔船购买甲壳类。
senses.why: Fisheries use the group name for the catch, so it doubles as a menu category.
senses.whyCN: 渔业用类群名指渔获，因此它同时成了菜单类别。

senses.title: The hard shell itself
senses.definition: the chitinous exoskeleton that a crustacean sheds as it grows
senses.definitionCN: 甲壳动物生长时蜕去的几丁质外骨骼
senses.example: The crustacean shell left behind was perfectly intact.
senses.exampleCN: 留下的甲壳完好无损。
senses.why: The shell is shed whole, so the word can name the casing apart from the animal.
senses.whyCN: 壳是整片蜕下的，因此这个词也能指脱离动物体的外壳。

senses.title: A fossil crustacean
senses.definition: ancient crustacean remains, common as microfossils in marine rocks
senses.definitionCN: 古代甲壳动物的遗骸，常以微体化石形式存在于海相岩石中
senses.example: Ostracods are tiny crustaceans used to date the core.
senses.exampleCN: 介形虫是微小的甲壳动物，用来给岩芯定年。
senses.why: Their shed shells fossilize well, which makes the group a geological tool.
senses.whyCN: 它们蜕下的壳容易形成化石，使这一类群成了地质工具。

senses.title: A parasitic crustacean
senses.definition: a crustacean that lives on or in another animal, such as a sea louse on a fish
senses.definitionCN: 附着在另一动物体表或体内生活的甲壳动物，如鱼身上的海虱
senses.example: Sea lice are crustaceans that damage farmed salmon.
senses.exampleCN: 海虱是危害养殖鲑鱼的甲壳动物。
senses.why: Parasitism evolved repeatedly in the group, so the word covers very different life habits.
senses.whyCN: 寄生在类群内多次演化出现，因此这个词涵盖差异极大的生活方式。

senses.title: A laboratory model
senses.definition: a crustacean used in research, such as Daphnia in toxicity tests
senses.definitionCN: 用于研究的甲壳动物，如毒性测试中的水蚤
senses.example: Daphnia is a crustacean used in standard toxicity tests.
senses.exampleCN: 水蚤是标准毒性测试中使用的一种甲壳动物。
senses.why: Short life cycles and sensitivity to chemicals make some crustaceans ideal test animals.
senses.whyCN: 生活史短、对化学品敏感，使某些甲壳动物成为理想的试验动物。

senses.title: A farmed crop
senses.definition: a crustacean raised in ponds or tanks for food
senses.definitionCN: 在池塘或水箱中为食用而养殖的甲壳动物
senses.example: Shrimp are the most valuable crustaceans in aquaculture.
senses.exampleCN: 虾是水产养殖中价值最高的甲壳类。
senses.why: Farming turns the animal into a commodity, and the group name becomes an industry label.
senses.whyCN: 养殖把动物变成商品，类群名也成了行业标签。

intro.en: Crustacean is built on Latin crusta 'crust, shell' plus the adjective ending -aceus, and entered English through scientific Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: crustacean 由拉丁 crusta「硬壳、外壳」加形容词词尾 -aceus 构成，经科学拉丁语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Crusta meant 'crust, rind, shell', the hard outer layer of bread or of an animal. Its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: crusta 意为「硬壳、外皮、外壳」，指面包或动物体表的硬层。其更深来源未有定论。

items.en: The adjective crustaceus 'having a crust or shell' was used for animals with hard coverings, not only for crabs.
items.cn: 形容词 crustaceus「有壳的」用于带硬覆盖的动物，并不只指蟹。

items.en: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century zoology raised Crustacea to a formal group name, separating crabs, shrimp and barnacles from insects.
items.cn: 18、19 世纪动物学把 Crustacea 提升为正式类群名，把蟹、虾、藤壶与昆虫分开。

items.en: English crustacean appears in the nineteenth century as the noun for a member of that group, alongside the older adjective crustaceous.
items.cn: 英语 crustacean 在 19 世纪作为该类群成员的名称出现，与更早的形容词 crustaceous 并存。

items.en: As seafood industries grew, crustacean became the neutral word for crabs and shrimp on menus and in regulations.
items.cn: 随着海产行业发展，crustacean 成了菜单与法规中对蟹、虾的中性称谓。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): crusta has no agreed etymology, so any pre-Latin form proposed for it is a reconstruction, not a documented word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：crusta 没有公认词源，凡为其提出的拉丁语之前形式都属重构，而非有记录的词。

note.en: Group one holds crust- words that look close but name shells, rocks or a geological period; group two holds animal-group words easily confused with crustacean.
note.cn: 第一组是同含 crust- 但指外壳、地壳或地质年代的形近词；第二组是易与甲壳动物混淆的动物类群词。

entries.definition: The hard outer layer of bread or rock; it is the source noun, not the animal.
entries.definitionCN: 面包或岩石的硬外层；它是来源名词，不是动物。

entries.definition: Meaning 'having a crust'; it describes the shell but does not name a crab or shrimp.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「有硬壳的」；它描述外壳，却不指蟹或虾。

entries.definition: Relating to the crust of the Earth; the same noun, an entirely different field.
entries.definitionCN: 与地壳有关的；同出一个名词，却属完全不同的领域。

entries.definition: The geological period named from Latin creta 'chalk', not crusta; the similar ending is a false friend.
entries.definitionCN: 地质年代名，来自拉丁 creta「白垩」，而非 crusta；词尾相似是假朋友。

entries.definition: Any jointed-legged invertebrate with an exoskeleton; crustaceans are one branch of the arthropods.
entries.definitionCN: 任何有外骨骼、具分节附肢的无脊椎动物；甲壳动物是节肢动物的一个分支。

entries.definition: A market term for edible crustaceans and mollusks together, broader and looser than crustacean.
entries.definitionCN: 市场用语，兼指可食甲壳动物与软体动物，比 crustacean 更宽泛、更松散。

entries.definition: A crustacean with ten legs, such as a crab or lobster; it is a subgroup, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 有十条腿的甲壳动物，如蟹或龙虾；它是亚群，并非同义词。

entries.definition: A crustacean that cements itself to rocks or hulls; it is a crustacean even though it looks like a shell.
entries.definitionCN: 把自己黏在岩石或船体上的甲壳动物；虽像贝壳，它仍是甲壳动物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: crust- means 'shell': a crustacean is the shelled animal.
normal.cn: crust- 意为「壳」：甲壳动物就是带壳的动物。

normal.en: Crabs, shrimp, lobsters and barnacles are all crustaceans, though they look very different.
normal.cn: 蟹、虾、龙虾、藤壶都是甲壳动物，尽管外形差异很大。

normal.en: A crustacean is an arthropod, but not every arthropod is a crustacean: insects and spiders are outside the group.
normal.cn: 甲壳动物是节肢动物，但并非所有节肢动物都是甲壳动物：昆虫与蜘蛛不在其中。

normal.en: Shellfish is the menu word; crustacean is the biological one.
normal.cn: shellfish 是菜单用语；crustacean 是生物学用语。

normal.en: Decapods are the ten-legged crustaceans, the ones most often eaten.
normal.cn: 十足目是有十条腿的甲壳动物，也是最常被食用的一类。

abstract.en: Picture an animal wearing its skeleton on the outside and shedding it to grow.
abstract.cn: 想象一个把骨骼穿在外面的动物，靠蜕掉它来长大。

abstract.en: Picture a barnacle that looks like a shell but is actually a shrimp glued down.
abstract.cn: 想象一只藤壶，看起来像贝壳，其实是一只黏住的虾。

abstract.en: Picture a microfossil the size of a pinhead dating a whole rock layer.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚针头大小的微体化石，为整层岩石定年。

examples.en: Crustaceans shed their shells several times before they reach adult size.
examples.cn: 甲壳动物在长到成体大小之前要蜕壳好几次。

examples.en: The trap caught crustaceans but no fish.
examples.cn: 这个陷阱只捕到甲壳类，没有鱼。

examples.en: Ocean acidification makes it harder for crustaceans to build their shells.
examples.cn: 海洋酸化使甲壳动物更难构建外壳。

dict_mnemonic.text: crust（硬壳）+ acean——带硬壳的一大类，就是甲壳动物；记「蟹虾都穿硬壳」

root: 拉丁 crusta「硬壳、外皮」→ crustaceus「有壳的」→ 近代拉丁 Crustacea；crusta 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a shelled animal through its roles: group member, collective group, seafood, shed shell, fossil, parasite, lab model and farmed crop.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一个带壳动物穿过各种角色：类群成员、整体类群、海产食物、蜕下的壳、化石、寄生虫、实验模型与养殖对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crab in a tide pool, its hard shell reflecting the water.
core.cn: 核心意象：潮池里的一只蟹，硬壳映着水光。

branches.en: ONE AND MANY: a single shelled animal, or the whole group treated as a unit.
branches.cn: 个体与整体：单个带壳动物，或把整个类群当作一个单位。

branches.en: COMMODITY: the same animal appears on a menu and in a farm pond.
branches.cn: 商品：同一种动物既出现在菜单上，也出现在养殖池里。

branches.en: THE CAST-OFF: the shell can be named apart from the living animal.
branches.cn: 蜕下之物：壳可以脱离活体单独被指称。

branches.en: EVIDENCE AND EXPERIMENT: shed shells become fossils; small species become test subjects.
branches.cn: 证据与实验：蜕壳变成化石；小型种类成为试验对象。

branches.en: THE OTHER LIFESTYLE: some crustaceans live on other animals.
branches.cn: 另一种活法：有些甲壳动物寄居在其他动物身上。

intro.en: Crustacean is a Latin-derived noun plus the English suffix -an; the stem is the same one that gives crust and crustal.
intro.cn: crustacean 是拉丁语源名词加英语后缀 -an；词干与 crust、crustal 相同。

latinIntro.en: Latin crusta gives crust, crustaceus and crustulum; crustaceus plus the group name Crustacea produced the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 crusta 衍生 crust、crustaceus 与 crustulum；crustaceus 加类群名 Crustacea 产生了英语名词。

items.example: The root supplies the shell image.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「壳」的形象。

items.example: Crustaceus means shell-covered.
A crustacean scuttled across the pool.
items.exampleCN: 一只甲壳动物横穿潮池。

items.example: Crustaceans crowded the bait.
The crustaceous covering protects the body.
The crust cracked under the tide.
Crustal movement raised the coast.
Crustacea is a large subphylum.
items.exampleCN: 甲壳类是一个很大的亚门。

definition_zh: adj. 笨重的，体积大的；厚实的（衣物）
definition_en: large and awkward to carry or move; thick because of heavy material or padding
core_image: 一件厚到让人打不开手臂的冬衣
scene: 冬天那件毛衣太厚，孩子裹在里面，动作慢了半拍。 The winter sweater was so bulky that the child moved in slow motion.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bulky 指体积大而笨重；句意是毛衣太厚，孩子裹在里面连动作都慢了。

pos.zh: 笨重的；体积大的；厚实的

senses.title: Large and hard to move
senses.definition: big enough that carrying it takes effort or two people
senses.definitionCN: 大到搬运费力或需要两个人
senses.example: The old printer was too bulky for the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 那台旧打印机太大，桌上放不下。
senses.why: Bulk is mass, and -y turns it into having too much mass for comfort.
senses.whyCN: bulk 是体积，-y 把它变成「体积大到不方便」。

senses.title: Thick and heavy to wear
senses.definition: made of thick material that gives the body extra width
senses.definitionCN: 用料厚实，使身体显得更宽
senses.example: He wore a bulky jacket over two shirts.
senses.exampleCN: 他在两件衬衫外又套了件厚夹克。
senses.why: Clothing borrowed the word once padding became the main reason a coat would not bend.
senses.whyCN: 当填充物成了外套不能弯折的主因，衣物也借用了这个词。

intro.en: Bulky is bulk plus -y; bulk first meant the cargo piled in a ship hold.
intro.cn: bulky 是 bulk 加 -y；bulk 最初指堆在船舱里的货物。

items.en: Bulki means a heap of cargo.
items.cn: bulki 意为成堆的货物。

items.en: Bulk names the mass of a ship cargo.
items.cn: bulk 指船货的整体体积。

items.en: Bulk extends to any large mass.
items.cn: 十六世纪扩大到任何大块物体。

items.en: The suffix -y makes bulky, full of bulk.
items.cn: 后缀 -y 构成 bulky，意为「体积满满」。

items.en: Coats and packs are called bulky.
items.cn: 十九世纪起用于描述外套与背包。

items.en: Bulky still means awkward rather than merely big.
items.cn: 现代仍强调「不便」而非仅仅「大」。

note.en: The look-alike group pairs bulky with words built on bulk or similar shapes; the near-meaning group ranks size from simply large to positively unwieldy.
note.cn: 形近组把 bulky 与 bulk 系列及形似词归在一起；近义组把「大」从单纯的大排到难搬动的累赘。

entries.definition: Great size or the main part.
entries.definitionCN: 体积；大部分。

entries.definition: Refusing to move or agree.
entries.definitionCN: 执拗不肯动的。

entries.definition: A wall between compartments on a ship.
entries.definitionCN: 船舱隔板。

entries.definition: A rounded glass lamp part.
entries.definitionCN: 灯泡。

entries.definition: Big in size or amount.
entries.definitionCN: 大的。

entries.definition: Very large and solid.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大的；厚重的。

entries.definition: Difficult to carry because of size.
entries.definitionCN: 累赘的；难搬的。

entries.definition: Difficult to hold or control.
entries.definitionCN: 难操控的。

normalIntro.en: Bulk is a heap, and bulky means having so much heap that it gets in the way.
normalIntro.cn: bulk 是一堆，bulky 就是「堆得太满反而碍事」。

normal.en: Bulk is the mass of a thing.
normal.cn: bulk 是一样东西的体积。

normal.en: Add -y and you have full of bulk.
normal.cn: 加上 -y 就是「满是体积」。

normal.en: A bulky box is wide and heavy.
normal.cn: bulky 的箱子又宽又重。

normal.en: A bulky coat makes your arms stick out.
normal.cn: bulky 的外套让手臂都合不拢。

normal.en: So bulky is big enough to be a nuisance.
normal.cn: 所以 bulky 是「大到碍事」。

abstract.en: Size that pushes back when you lift it.
abstract.cn: 你一抬它就往回坠的体积。

abstract.en: A shape too wide for its own doorway.
abstract.cn: 宽得进不去自家门框的形状。

abstract.en: Mass without malice, still in the way.
abstract.cn: 没有恶意却挡路的重量。

examples.en: The drill is bulky but it never jams.
examples.cn: 这台钻机很笨重，但从不卡壳。

examples.en: She packs light and avoids bulky items.
examples.cn: 她行李精简，不带大件。

examples.en: The old television was too bulky for the small room.
examples.cn: 那台旧电视太占地方，小房间放不下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「背包」——背包塞满就变成又大又重的东西。

root: bulk（堆、体积）+ -y（充满……的）

sensesIntro.en: Whether it is a printer or a sweater, bulky describes the same failure: the object takes more room than the task needs.
sensesIntro.cn: 无论是打印机还是毛衣，bulky 描述的是同一种不便：物体占的地方超过了事情需要的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coat so thick that the arms cannot hang straight
core.cn: 核心意象：厚到手臂都垂不直的外套

branches.en: A printer wider than the desk.
branches.cn: 比桌子还宽的打印机。

branches.en: A case two people must lift.
branches.cn: 要两个人抬的箱子。

branches.en: A padded coat in January.
branches.cn: 一月里那件填充厚实的外套。

branches.en: Mittens that will not grip.
branches.cn: 握不住东西的厚手套。

branches.en: Too much material for the job.
branches.cn: 为这件事准备了太多材料。

intro.en: Bulky is bulk plus -y; the list below covers that suffix and the vocabulary of size, mass and awkward weight.
intro.cn: bulky 是 bulk 加 -y；下面列出这个后缀以及「体积、质量、笨重」词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin massa is a lump, volumen is a roll, and gravis is heavy.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 massa 意为团块，volumen 意为卷，gravis 意为沉重。

items.example: bulky, bulk
bulky, heavy
bulkier, heavier
bulkiest, heaviest
bulkiness, heaviness
massive, mass
massive, passive
volume, voluminous

latinEntries.exampleCN: massa 产生 mass 与 massive。
volumen 产生 volume 与 voluminous。
gravis 产生 gravity 与 grave。

definition_zh: 机械工程；设计、制造与维护机器及动力系统的工程分支
definition_en: the branch of engineering that designs, builds and maintains machines, mechanisms and power systems
core_image: 车间里立着一台拆开的发动机，旁边摊着热力学图表与零件清单，工程师正把两者对照
scene: 车间里立着一台拆开的发动机，旁边摊着图表与零件清单，有人正把两者逐一对照。 Mechanical engineering turned the noisy engine into a quieter one without losing power.
sceneCN: 这里 mechanical engineering 指设计、制造与维护机器及动力系统的工程分支（第 1 个义项：这一分支）；句意：机械工程把那台吵闹的发动机改得更安静，却没有损失动力。

pos.zh: 机械工程；机械工程学（作定语）

senses.title: The branch that designs machines
senses.definition: the division of engineering concerned with machines, their parts and their motion
senses.definitionCN: 工程中负责机器、其部件及其运动的门类
senses.example: Mechanical engineering begins where parts have to move without breaking.
senses.exampleCN: 机械工程从「部件必须动而不坏」这一点开始。
senses.why: the compound narrows a wide profession to the part that deals with moving hardware.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把宽泛的行业收窄到处理运动硬件的那一部分。

senses.title: The profession of its practitioners
senses.definition: the work and career of the engineers who practise this branch
senses.definitionCN: 从事这一分支的工程师的工作与职业
senses.example: Mechanical engineering kept the factory running through two recessions.
senses.exampleCN: 机械工程让那家工厂熬过了两次衰退。
senses.why: a branch is also a body of people, and the phrase names their livelihood.
senses.whyCN: 分支同时也是一群人，这个短语就指他们的生计。

senses.title: The practice of designing power and motion
senses.titleCN: 设计动力与运动系统的实务
senses.definition: the applied work of sizing motors, shafts, bearings and transmissions
senses.definitionCN: 确定电机、轴、轴承与传动尺寸的应用工作
senses.example: Mechanical engineering chose the bearing that outlasted the warranty.
senses.exampleCN: 机械工程选用了寿命超过保修期的轴承。
senses.why: the discipline's daily decisions are about power and motion, so the phrase often means that practice.
senses.whyCN: 这门学问的日常决策围绕动力与运动，因此短语常指这项实务。

senses.title: A university department and degree
senses.definition: the academic unit and programme that teach the branch
senses.definitionCN: 讲授这一分支的学术单位与培养项目
senses.example: The mechanical engineering department opened a new heat lab.
senses.exampleCN: 机械工程系新开了一间热学实验室。
senses.why: codified knowledge taught in one place becomes an institution with a name.
senses.whyCN: 被整理的知识在一处讲授，就变成有名目的建制。

senses.title: An industry sector
senses.definition: the firms that build machines and mechanical systems for a market
senses.definitionCN: 为市场制造机器与机械系统的公司群体
senses.example: Mechanical engineering employs a third of the town.
senses.exampleCN: 机械工程养活了镇上三分之一的人。
senses.why: a profession counted in output and jobs becomes a sector in economic language.
senses.whyCN: 被按产值与岗位统计的职业，在经济语言里就成了产业部门。

senses.title: Thermodynamics and machine theory
senses.definition: the core knowledge of heat, energy and mechanisms that the branch rests on
senses.definitionCN: 该分支所依托的热、能量与机构的核心知识
senses.example: Mechanical engineering still rewards those who understand cycles.
senses.exampleCN: 机械工程仍然厚待懂循环过程的人。
senses.why: the branch's identity is fixed by the sciences it applies, especially heat and mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 这一分支的身份由它所应用的学问固定，尤其是热与机构。

senses.title: Manufacturing system design
senses.definition: the planning of production machines and the lines that link them
senses.definitionCN: 规划生产机器以及连接它们的产线
senses.example: Mechanical engineering laid out the line before the robots arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 机械工程在机器人到来之前就排好了产线。
senses.why: machines are rarely alone, and arranging them into a working line belongs to the same branch.
senses.whyCN: 机器很少孤立存在，把它们排成能运转的产线也属同一分支。

senses.title: A curriculum of study
senses.definition: the sequence of courses that turns a student into a practitioner
senses.definitionCN: 把学生培养成从业者的课程序列
senses.example: The curriculum in mechanical engineering moved drafting into the first term.
senses.exampleCN: 机械工程的课程把制图挪到了第一学期。
senses.why: the taught order of the branch is itself called by its name.
senses.whyCN: 这一分支的教学顺序本身也用它的名字来称呼。

intro.en: Mechanical engineering joins a Greek word for device with a French-shaped word for the building profession. The phrase names the oldest of the engineering branches.
intro.cn: mechanical engineering 把希腊语「装置」与法语形态的「建造行业」拼在一起。这个短语命名了工程中最古老的分支。

items.en: Greek mekhane meant device or means, and its adjective mekhanikos passed through Latin as mechanicus.
items.cn: 希腊语 mekhane 指装置或手段，其形容词 mekhanikos 经拉丁语成为 mechanicus。

items.en: English mechanical named what belongs to machines and to the science of force and motion.
items.cn: 英语 mechanical 指属于机器以及力与运动的学问。

items.en: Engine, from ingenium, meant a contrivance before it meant a motor, and its builders were the first engineers.
items.cn: engine 来自 ingenium，先指巧妙装置，后指发动机，其建造者是最早的工程师。

items.en: Engineering became a profession with canals, roads and steam, and machine work became its largest branch.
items.cn: 随着运河、道路与蒸汽，工程成为职业，机器工作成为其中最大的分支。

items.en: Technical schools separated machine building from civil works, and the compound became the branch's fixed name.
items.cn: 技术学校把机器制造与土木分开，这个复合词就成了该分支的固定名称。

items.en: The branch later absorbed thermodynamics, control and manufacturing systems while keeping the old name.
items.cn: 这一分支后来吸收热力学、控制与制造系统，却保留了旧名称。

note.en: The first group is the words inside the phrase and their close forms; the second group is neighbouring engineering branches.
note.cn: 第一组是短语内部的词及其近形；第二组是相邻的工程分支。

entries.definition: Belonging to machines or done without thought; alone it does not name a branch of study.
entries.definitionCN: 指属于机器或不假思索；单独用时并不指某个学科分支。

entries.definition: The practitioner of the branch; the phrase names the field rather than its worker.
entries.definitionCN: 指这一分支的从业者；短语指领域而非从业者。

entries.definition: The general field; the compound selects the machine-building part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指整个行业；复合词选取其中造机器的部分。

entries.definition: An assembly of moving parts; it is one of the things this branch designs.
entries.definitionCN: 指运动部件的组合；它是这一分支所设计的东西之一。

entries.definition: The branch for roads, bridges and buildings; both trace back to the same profession.
entries.definitionCN: 负责道路、桥梁与建筑的分支；两者都出自同一行业。

entries.definition: The branch for electrical systems; machines often need both branches at once.
entries.definitionCN: 负责电气系统的分支；机器常常同时需要两个分支。

entries.definition: The joining of machine design with electronics and control; a later blend beside the older branch.
entries.definitionCN: 把机械设计与电子、控制结合；是旧分支旁边较晚的混合领域。

entries.definition: The design of production systems and work methods rather than the machines themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 设计生产系统与工作方法，而不是机器本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the two real halves and the real academic phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自两个真实构件与真实学术搭配。

normal.en: Mekhane is a device and ingenium is talent, so the phrase is device work done by trained talent.
normal.cn: mekhane 是装置，ingenium 是才能，所以这个短语是「由受过训练的才能所做的装置工作」。

normal.en: It is the branch that deals with things that move and can break.
normal.cn: 它是处理「会动、也会坏」的东西的那个分支。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: mechanical engineering degree, mechanical engineering department.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：机械工程学位、机械工程系。

normal.en: Its sibling branches are civil and electrical, and the three often share a project.
normal.cn: 它的兄弟分支是土木与电气，三者常常共用同一个项目。

normal.en: The person is a mechanical engineer; the field keeps the longer phrase.
normal.cn: 人叫 mechanical engineer，领域则用更长的短语。

abstract.en: Picture an engine opened like a book, its diagrams laid beside the parts they describe.
abstract.cn: 想象一台发动机像书一样被翻开，图表摊在它所描述的零件旁边。

abstract.en: Picture a bearing that quietly outlives every promise made about it.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚轴承，静静地比所有关于它的承诺活得都久。

abstract.en: Picture a factory line drawn on paper years before the machines arrive.
abstract.cn: 想象一条在机器到来数年前就画在纸上的产线。

examples.en: Mechanical engineering solved the vibration by changing a single bearing.
examples.cn: 机械工程换了一枚轴承就解决了振动问题。

examples.en: She chose mechanical engineering because she wanted to hold what she designed.
examples.cn: 她选择机械工程，因为她想亲手拿起自己设计的东西。

examples.en: The department merged mechanical engineering with materials science.
examples.cn: 那个系把机械工程与材料科学合并了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米卡你扣（mechanical）恩机捏 ring（engineering）」——米粒卡住扣子的地方，正是机械工程要修的地方

root: 希腊 mekhane「装置」→ mechanicus → mechanical；拉丁 ingenium「才能」→ engine → engineer → engineering；十九世纪技术学校分科后合成 mechanical engineering。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses cover the branch, its practitioners, power-and-motion practice, the department, the sector, core theory, production lines and the curriculum.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项涵盖分支本身、从业者、动力与运动实务、院系、产业、核心理论、产线与课程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an opened engine beside heat charts and a parts list, being checked item by item.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台拆开的发动机旁边摊着热学图表与零件清单，正被逐项核对。

branches.en: BRANCH AND THEORY: the division itself, and the heat-and-mechanism knowledge it rests on.
branches.cn: 分支与理论：这一门类本身，以及它所依托的热与机构知识。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND TEACHING: the practitioners' livelihood, and the course sequence that produces them.
branches.cn: 人与教学：从业者的生计，以及培养他们的课程序列。

branches.en: POWER AND MOTION PRACTICE: sizing motors, shafts, bearings and drives.
branches.cn: 动力与运动实务：确定电机、轴、轴承与传动的尺寸。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: a department and a degree with a fixed name.
branches.cn: 建制：有名目的院系与学位。

branches.en: SCALE AND ARRANGEMENT: an economic sector on one side, production lines on the other.
branches.cn: 规模与安排：一边是产业部门，一边是生产产线。

intro.en: The phrase is two nouns, each already formed; joining them adds no affix but narrows a profession to one branch.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个已成形名词组成；并置不添加词缀，只是把行业收窄为一个分支。

latinIntro.en: Greek mekhane reaches English through Latin mechanicus, and Latin ingenium through French engin; the English endings -ical and -ing close both halves.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 mekhane 经拉丁语 mechanicus 进入英语，拉丁语 ingenium 经法语 engin 进入英语；两半各以英语词尾 -ical 与 -ing 收束。

items.example: The noun is the source of the first half.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是第一半的来源。

items.example: The ending makes the first half an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把前半变成形容词。

items.example: The noun sits behind the second half.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词位于后半的背后。

items.example: The intermediate form links talent to machinery.
items.exampleCN: 这个中间形式把才能与机械连起来。

items.example: The ending marks the practitioner.
The ending turns the practitioner into a profession.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把从业者变成一门职业。

items.example: The prefix marks the heat side of the branch.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记该分支的热学一面。

items.example: The form appears in names of machine-based fields.
items.exampleCN: 这个构词成分出现在以机器为基础的领域名称中。

definition_zh: 生物工程；把工程原理用于生物系统与医学
definition_en: the application of engineering principles and methods to biological systems and medicine
core_image: 工程师的图纸上画着细胞、血管与人造关节
scene: 这里指「生物工程」。 Bioengineering students built a scaffold on which new skin could grow.
sceneCN: 这里 bioengineering 指「组织工程」（第 2 个义项：用工程支架让活组织再生）；句意：生物工程专业的学生搭建了一个能让新皮肤生长的支架。

pos.zh: 生物工程；生物工程学；生物医学工程（不可数）

derivatives.zh: 生物工程师；用生物工程改造

senses.title: Engineering for living systems
senses.titleCN: 面向生命系统的工程学
senses.definition: the application of engineering principles to biological systems and to medicine
senses.definitionCN: 把工程原理应用于生物系统与医学
senses.example: Bioengineering combines mechanics, materials and cell biology.
senses.exampleCN: 生物工程把力学、材料学与细胞生物学结合起来。
senses.why: The word simply joins engineering to life: the methods are those of the engineer, and the object is a living system.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把工程学与生命直接拼在一起：方法来自工程师，对象是生命系统。

senses.title: Tissue and organ engineering
senses.definition: the branch that builds scaffolds and living substitutes for damaged tissue or organs
senses.definitionCN: 构建支架与活体替代物、修复受损组织或器官的分支
senses.example: Bioengineering has produced lab-grown cartilage for knee repair.
senses.exampleCN: 生物工程已经造出用于膝关节修复的实验室培育软骨。
senses.why: Rebuilding a body part requires both a design and living cells, so this branch is the clearest meeting point of the two halves of the word.
senses.whyCN: 重建身体部件既需要设计，也需要活细胞，因此这一分支是「工程」与「生命」两半最直接的汇合处。

senses.title: Genetic engineering
senses.definition: the deliberate modification of an organism's genetic material
senses.definitionCN: 有目的地改造生物体的遗传物质
senses.example: Bioengineering of the yeast let it produce a new medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 对酵母的基因工程改造使它能够生产一种新药。
senses.why: At the molecular scale, engineering becomes the rewriting of DNA, and popular usage often treats bioengineering and genetic engineering as interchangeable.
senses.whyCN: 在分子尺度上，工程就变成改写 DNA，因此通俗用法常把生物工程与基因工程当作同义词。

senses.title: Medical devices and prosthetics
senses.definition: the design of implants, prostheses and machines that work with the body
senses.definitionCN: 设计与身体配合的植入物、假体与机器
senses.example: Bioengineering developed the artificial heart valve used in the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 生物工程研制了试验中使用的人工心脏瓣膜。
senses.why: An engineer who builds a device for a body must respect biological constraints, which is exactly what the compound promises.
senses.whyCN: 为身体制造装置的工程师必须服从生物约束，这正是这个复合词所承诺的内容。

senses.title: Agricultural engineering
senses.definition: the engineering of crops and farm animals for yield, resistance or quality
senses.definitionCN: 为提高产量、抗性或品质而对作物与畜禽进行的工程改造
senses.example: Bioengineering gave the rice a gene for salt tolerance.
senses.exampleCN: 生物工程赋予这种水稻一个耐盐基因。
senses.why: Farming has always shaped living things; modern tools turn that shaping into a branch of engineering.
senses.whyCN: 农业一直在塑造生物；现代工具把这种塑造变成了工程学的一个分支。

senses.title: Environmental engineering
senses.definition: the use of engineered organisms or systems to clean up pollution
senses.definitionCN: 利用经改造的生物或系统治理污染
senses.example: Bioengineering produced bacteria that digest oil spills.
senses.exampleCN: 生物工程造出了能分解泄漏石油的细菌。
senses.why: The same design logic is pointed at waste and pollution, so the word gains an environmental application.
senses.whyCN: 同一套设计逻辑被指向废物与污染，于是这个词获得了环境方面的应用义。

senses.title: The field or department
senses.definition: the academic discipline or the department that teaches and researches it
senses.definitionCN: 教授与研究该方向的学科或院系
senses.example: The bioengineering department shares a building with the medical school.
senses.exampleCN: 生物工程系与医学院共用一栋楼。
senses.why: As with every discipline name, the word stands for the institution and the people who practise it.
senses.whyCN: 和所有学科名一样，这个词也代指机构与从事它的人。

senses.title: Designing biological parts
senses.definition: the design of biological parts or systems that do not exist in nature
senses.definitionCN: 设计自然界并不存在的生物部件或系统
senses.example: Bioengineering now writes circuits into bacterial DNA.
senses.exampleCN: 生物工程如今把逻辑回路写进细菌的 DNA。
senses.why: Once living parts are treated as components, the engineer's verb 'design' applies to biology itself, the sense closest to synthetic biology.
senses.whyCN: 一旦生命的部件被当作零件，工程师的动词「设计」就能用于生物学本身，这是最接近合成生物学的义项。

intro.en: Bioengineering is a 20th-century compound: a Greek prefix for life attached to an English noun whose roots reach Latin and French.
intro.cn: bioengineering 是 20 世纪的复合词：表示生命的希腊语前缀，加上一个词源可追溯至拉丁语与法语的英语名词。

items.en: bio- comes from Greek bios, 'life'. It became a standard scientific prefix in the 19th century.
items.cn: bio- 出自希腊语 bios「生命」，在 19 世纪成为标准的科学前缀。

items.en: Engineering goes back to engine, from Old French engin and Latin ingenium, 'native talent, clever device'. The modern sense of designing machines is 18th and 19th century.
items.cn: engineering 经古法语 engin 上溯至拉丁语 ingenium「天赋、巧妙的装置」。设计机器的现代义形成于 18 至 19 世纪。

items.en: The compound bioengineering is generally dated to the mid-20th century, when engineering methods were first applied systematically to medicine and living tissue. The exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: bioengineering 这一复合词一般认为出现于 20 世纪中叶，当时工程方法开始被系统地用于医学与活组织。确切的首见出处不确定。

items.en: In the 1960s and 1970s the term became institutional, with departments, journals and degree programmes.
items.cn: 1960 至 1970 年代，这个词逐渐制度化，出现了系所、期刊与学位项目。

items.en: After the 1970s, recombinant DNA widened bioengineering to mean genetic modification, and later synthetic biology.
items.cn: 1970 年代以后，重组 DNA 使 bioengineering 扩展到基因改造，后来又延伸到合成生物学。

note.en: The first group separates neighbouring compounds built on bio-; the second separates engineering from the sciences it borrows from.
note.cn: 第一组区分以 bio- 构成的邻近复合词；第二组把工程学与它所借用的科学区分开。

entries.definition: The use of living systems to make products; it overlaps with bioengineering but stresses production rather than engineering design.
entries.definitionCN: 指利用生命系统制造产品，与生物工程重叠，但更强调生产而不是工程设计。

entries.definition: The part of bioengineering concerned with medicine and health care; it is narrower than the general term.
entries.definitionCN: 生物工程中面向医学与医疗保健的部分，比总称更窄。

entries.definition: The direct alteration of DNA; it is one branch of bioengineering, not a synonym for the whole field.
entries.definitionCN: 指直接改造 DNA，是生物工程的一个分支，并不等同于整个领域。

entries.definition: The design and building of machines, structures and systems; bioengineering is its living and medical application.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指机器、结构与系统的设计与建造；生物工程是它在生命与医学领域的应用。

entries.definition: The study of biological systems with physics methods; it explains how life obeys physical laws rather than designing new parts.
entries.definitionCN: 用物理学方法研究生物系统，解释生命如何服从物理规律，而不是设计新部件。

entries.definition: The design and construction of new biological parts and systems, often seen as the engineering wing of biology.
entries.definitionCN: 设计与构建新的生物部件与系统，常被视为生物学的工程分支。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: bio- 'life' + engineering: engineering aimed at living systems.
normal.cn: bio-「生命」+ engineering「工程」：对准生命系统的工程。

normal.en: The family runs bioengineer, bioengineered, bioreactor and biomedical engineering.
normal.cn: 同族词有 bioengineer、bioengineered、bioreactor、biomedical engineering。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: tissue bioengineering, plant bioengineering, bioengineering department.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：组织生物工程、植物生物工程、生物工程系。

normal.en: The two halves are visible: life on the left, design on the right.
normal.cn: 两半都看得见：左边是生命，右边是设计。

normal.en: A bioreactor is the factory floor where engineered cells do their work.
normal.cn: 生物反应器就是经改造的细胞干活的车间。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge made of cells: the engineer draws it, the biologist grows it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座用细胞搭成的桥：工程师画图，生物学家把它长出来。

abstract.en: A scaffold for tissue is a trellis for a climbing plant, except the plant is human skin.
abstract.cn: 组织支架就像给攀援植物搭的棚架，只不过这株植物是人的皮肤。

abstract.en: Genetic engineering is editing a recipe that writes itself.
abstract.cn: 基因工程就是修改一份会自己书写的食谱。

examples.en: Bioengineering combines materials science with cell biology.
examples.cn: 生物工程把材料科学与细胞生物学结合起来。

examples.en: The lab uses bioengineering to grow replacement blood vessels.
examples.cn: 该实验室用生物工程培育替代血管。

examples.en: Critics argue that bioengineering of crops should be labelled clearly.
examples.cn: 批评者认为，对作物进行生物工程改造应当明确标注。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「bio（生命）+ engineering（工程）」→ 给生命做工程 → 生物工程

root: 希腊语 bios「生命」+ engineering（经古法语 engin 上溯至拉丁语 ingenium「天赋、巧妙的装置」），20 世纪合成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses extend engineering into life: from the general field to tissue, genes, devices, farms, pollution, institutions, and finally the design of entirely new biological parts.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把工程学伸进生命：从总领域到组织、基因、器械、农业、污染治理、院系，最后到设计全新的生物部件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an engineer's drawing in which the parts are cells, vessels and joints.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张工程师的图纸，上面的零件是细胞、血管与关节。

branches.en: THE GENERAL FIELD: engineering methods applied to any living system.
branches.cn: 总领域：工程方法用于任何生命系统。

branches.en: REPAIR: scaffolds and implants that restore or replace body parts.
branches.cn: 修复：恢复或替代身体部件的支架与植入物。

branches.en: REWRITE: genetic engineering works at the level of DNA.
branches.cn: 改写：基因工程在 DNA 层面操作。

branches.en: BEYOND MEDICINE: crops and microbes are engineered for food and for cleanup.
branches.cn: 医学之外：作物与微生物被改造用于粮食与污染治理。

branches.en: INSTITUTION AND INVENTION: the department that practises it, and the design of parts nature never made.
branches.cn: 机构与发明：从事它的院系，以及设计自然界从未有过的部件。

intro.en: Bioengineering joins a Greek prefix for life to an English verbal noun; the suffix -ing turns the engineer's work into a field.
intro.cn: bioengineering 把表示生命的希腊语前缀接到一个英语动名词上；后缀 -ing 把工程师的工作变成一个领域。

latinIntro.en: Greek bios supplies bio-. Latin ingenium, through Old French engin, supplies the engineering element; the -ing suffix is English.
latinIntro.cn: bio- 来自希腊语 bios；engineering 的成分来自拉丁语 ingenium，经古法语 engin 进入英语；-ing 是英语后缀。

items.meaningCN: 应用于生命系统的工程学
items.example: Bioengineering offers a route to lab-grown organs.
items.exampleCN: 生物工程为实验室培育器官提供了一条路径。

items.meaning: a person who engineers living systems
items.meaningCN: 对生命系统进行工程改造的人
items.example: The bioengineer adjusted the scaffold's stiffness.
items.exampleCN: 生物工程师调整了支架的硬度。

items.example: The supermarket sells bioengineered salmon.
items.exampleCN: 这家超市出售经生物工程改造的三文鱼。

items.meaning: a vessel in which living cells make a product
items.meaningCN: 活细胞在其中生产产品的容器
items.example: The bioreactor produced antibodies for a year.
items.exampleCN: 这个生物反应器生产了一年抗体。

items.meaning: relating to biology and medicine together
items.meaningCN: 同时涉及生物学与医学的
items.example: Biomedical engineers design artificial joints.
items.exampleCN: 生物医学工程师设计人工关节。

items.meaning: the design and building of machines and systems
items.meaningCN: 机器与系统的设计与建造
items.example: Engineering turned the idea into a working device.
items.exampleCN: 工程学把这个想法变成了可用的装置。

items.meaning: a person who designs machines or systems
items.example: The engineer checked the load on the implant.
items.exampleCN: 工程师检查了植入物承受的载荷。

items.example: Genetic engineering edits the instructions of a cell.
items.exampleCN: 基因工程编辑细胞的指令。

items.meaning: a temporary frame that supports growth
items.example: Cells colonise the scaffold within days.
items.exampleCN: 细胞在几天内就占领了支架。

definition_zh: 大陆冰盖；冰盖
definition_en: a mass of glacial ice covering a large area of land and spreading outward under its own weight
core_image: 一整块厚冰铺满大陆，边缘像糖浆一样向外缓慢摊开
scene: 飞机越过格陵兰上空，窗外是一整片没有尽头的白色，只有边缘露出黑色岩脊。 Below them the ice sheet stretched to the horizon.
sceneCN: 这里 ice sheet 指「大陆冰盖」（第 1 个义项：覆盖大片陆地、靠自身重量向外流动的巨厚冰体）；句意为他们脚下的冰盖一直铺到天边。

pos.zh: 大陆冰盖；冰盖（可数，复数 ice sheets）

derivatives.zh: ice（复合词前项，古英语 īs，无后缀）→ 冰
ic-（ice 去 -e）+ -y（古英语 -ig，形容词后缀）→ 像冰一样的：结冰的、冰冷的
sheet（复合词后项，古英语 scēte，无后缀）→ 片；层；床单
ice + field（复合术语，无后缀）→ 连片冰区：冰原
ice + cap（复合术语，无后缀；cap 上溯晚期拉丁 cappa「头巾」）→ 覆于山顶或极区的穹状冰：冰帽

senses.title: A continental ice mass
senses.titleCN: 大陆冰盖：覆盖大陆的巨厚冰体
senses.definition: a mass of ice covering a large land area and flowing outward under its own weight
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖大片陆地、靠自身重量向外流动的巨大冰体
senses.example: Below them the ice sheet stretched to the horizon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们脚下的冰盖一直铺到天边。
senses.why: sheet names a broad flat layer, and ice supplies the material; the compound is literally a sheet made of ice.
senses.whyCN: sheet 命名宽而平的层，ice 提供材料；这个复合词字面上就是「冰做的层」。

senses.title: The thickness and mass
senses.definition: the body of ice considered as a volume with depth and mass
senses.definitionCN: 把冰体视为有厚度与质量的体积
senses.example: The ice sheet is almost three kilometres thick at its centre.
senses.exampleCN: 冰盖中心处厚近三公里。
senses.why: a sheet can be measured in thickness, so the word names a volume rather than only a surface.
senses.whyCN: 一层东西可以按厚度测量，因此这个词命名体积，而不只是表面。

senses.title: The area covered
senses.definition: the extent of land buried under the ice sheet
senses.definitionCN: 被冰盖掩埋的土地范围
senses.example: The ice sheet covers most of the island.
senses.exampleCN: 冰盖覆盖了该岛的大部分。
senses.why: the sheet also has a footprint, and geography names the land it buries.
senses.whyCN: 冰盖还有覆盖范围，地理学命名它所掩埋的土地。

senses.title: An ancient ice sheet
senses.definition: an ice sheet of an earlier glaciation, known from deposits and landforms
senses.definitionCN: 更早冰期的冰盖，由沉积与地貌得知
senses.example: The Laurentide ice sheet once covered northern North America.
senses.exampleCN: 劳伦泰德冰盖曾经覆盖北美北部。
senses.why: past sheets are known from the deposits they left, so the word extends to ice that no longer exists.
senses.whyCN: 过去的冰盖由留下的沉积得知，因此这个词扩展到已不存在的冰。

senses.title: Mass balance and loss
senses.definition: the balance between snow added and ice lost through melting and calving
senses.definitionCN: 新增积雪与融化、崩解所失冰量之间的平衡
senses.example: The ice sheet loses mass faster than snow can replace it.
senses.exampleCN: 冰盖失去质量的速度快于积雪补充。
senses.why: a mass that gains snow and loses ice is treated as a budget, which is why mass balance is a standard phrase.
senses.whyCN: 既得雪又失冰的冰体被当作一份收支，因此 质量平衡（mass balance） 成为固定说法。

senses.title: The margin of the ice
senses.definition: the outer edge where the ice sheet meets rock, sea or meltwater
senses.definitionCN: 冰盖与岩石、海洋或融水相接的外缘
senses.example: Meltwater ponds form along the ice sheet margin.
senses.exampleCN: 融水塘沿冰盖边缘形成。
senses.why: the margin is where ice meets rock, sea or melt, so the word names that boundary zone.
senses.whyCN: 边缘是冰与岩石、海或融水相接之处，因此这个词命名那条边界带。

senses.title: Ice as a climate archive
senses.definition: the ice sheet read as a record of past atmospheres in trapped air and layers
senses.definitionCN: 把冰盖读作封存空气与层序的古代大气记录
senses.example: Air bubbles in the ice sheet record ancient atmospheres.
senses.exampleCN: 冰盖中的气泡记录着古代大气。
senses.why: trapped air and annual layers make the ice a readable archive, so the word acquires a scientific sense as record.
senses.whyCN: 被封存的空气与年层使冰成为可读的档案，因此这个词获得「记录」的科学义。

senses.title: A polar cap on another planet
senses.titleCN: 行星科学：其他行星的极地冰盖
senses.definition: a large permanent ice deposit at the pole of another planet
senses.definitionCN: 另一颗行星极区的大型永久冰沉积
senses.example: Mars has ice sheets at both poles.
senses.exampleCN: 火星两极都有冰盖。
senses.why: the same morphology appears on Mars, so the term is extended beyond Earth.
senses.whyCN: 同样的形态在火星出现，因此这个术语被扩展到地球之外。

intro.en: Ice sheet is an English compound of ice and sheet. Ice goes back to Old English is, and sheet to Old English scete, a piece of cloth. The geological sense is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ice sheet 是英语复合词，由 ice 与 sheet 构成。ice 上承古英语 is，sheet 上承古英语 scete「一块布」。地质义是近代的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Is is the Germanic word for ice, with German Eis and Dutch ijs as close relatives.
items.cn: is 是日耳曼语的冰词，德语 Eis 与荷兰语 ijs 是近亲。

items.en: Scete meant a piece of cloth or a corner, and later a broad flat layer of any material, such as a sheet of paper or metal.
items.cn: scete 指一块布或一角，后来指任何材料的宽平层，如一张纸或一块金属板。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geologists needed a term for ice that covers a continent rather than a valley, and borrowed the image of a sheet laid over the land.
items.cn: 19 世纪地质学家需要一个词指覆盖大陆而非山谷的冰，于是借用「铺在陆地上的层」这一意象。

items.en: By the twentieth century an ice sheet is defined technically: it covers more than fifty thousand square kilometres and spreads under its own weight.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪，冰盖有了技术定义：面积超过五万平方公里，并靠自身重量向外摊开。

items.en: Ice sheet mass balance, ice cores and sea-level contribution become central measures in late twentieth-century climate research.
items.cn: 冰盖质量平衡、冰芯与对海平面的贡献成为 20 世纪后期气候研究的核心指标。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the two words are securely documented, but the compound's earliest citation is dated differently in different references.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：两个词均有可靠记载，但复合词的最早书证各家年代不一。

note.en: Group one holds the ice bodies that are constantly mistaken for one another; group two holds the wider terms of ice masses and ice movement.
note.cn: 第一组是常被互相认错的各类冰体；第二组是冰体与冰流的更宽术语。

entries.definition: A dome of ice over a summit or polar region, smaller than an ice sheet and not spreading over a continent.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖山顶或极地区域的穹状冰体，比冰盖小，也不铺满大陆。

entries.definition: A thick floating plate of ice attached to a coast; it is seaward of an ice sheet, not on land.
entries.definitionCN: 附着海岸、漂浮的厚冰板；它在冰盖靠海一侧，并不在陆地上。

entries.definition: A network of glaciers covering a mountain region, smaller and more broken than an ice sheet.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖山区的冰川网络，比冰盖小且更破碎。

entries.definition: Frozen seawater at the surface of the ocean; it floats and is not land ice.
entries.definitionCN: 海面冻结的海水；它漂浮着，并非陆地冰。

entries.definition: A body of ice confined by topography and flowing down a valley or out of an ice sheet.
entries.definitionCN: 受地形约束、沿谷下行或从冰盖流出的冰体。

entries.definition: Any large body of ice, used when size or type does not need to be specified.
entries.definitionCN: 任何大型冰体，用于无需指明大小或类型时。

entries.definition: A rapidly moving channel within an ice sheet, draining it like a river drains a basin.
entries.definitionCN: 冰盖内部快速流动的通道，像河流排干盆地一样排走冰。

entries.definition: Ice at either pole, whether on land or on sea; the term says where, not what shape.
entries.definitionCN: 两极的冰，无论在陆上还是海上；这个词说的是位置，而非形态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds and real neighbours, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合词与邻近术语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ice + sheet: a sheet of ice laid over a continent.
normal.cn: ice + sheet：铺在大陆上的一层冰。

normal.en: Size order: ice cap, ice field, ice sheet, with the sheet the largest and the cap the smallest.
normal.cn: 大小次序：冰帽、冰原、冰盖，冰盖最大，冰帽最小。

normal.en: An ice sheet rests on land; an ice shelf floats on sea. The second word tells you which.
normal.cn: 冰盖架在陆地上，冰架浮在海上；第二个词告诉你属于哪一种。

normal.en: Greenland and Antarctica each have one great ice sheet, which is why the names are fixed phrases.
normal.cn: 格陵兰与南极各有一块巨大冰盖，因此相关说法是固定短语。

normal.en: Ice sheet mass balance is income of snow minus loss of melt and calving.
normal.cn: 冰盖质量平衡就是积雪的收入减去融化与崩解的支出。

abstract.en: An ice sheet is a continent wearing its winter as a second skin.
abstract.cn: 冰盖是一块大陆把冬天当作第二层皮肤穿着。

abstract.en: An archive written in ice can be read only by melting it, which is the archive's danger.
abstract.cn: 以冰写成的档案只有融化才能读取，而这正是档案的危险。

abstract.en: Slow masses decide coastlines: an ice sheet can raise the sea without a single storm.
abstract.cn: 缓慢的巨物决定海岸线：一块冰盖不用一场风暴就能抬高海面。

examples.en: The Greenland ice sheet is losing mass every year.
examples.cn: 格陵兰冰盖每年都在失去质量。

examples.en: Scientists drill ice cores through the ice sheet.
examples.cn: 科学家钻透冰盖取冰芯。

examples.en: The ice sheet covered the continent during the last glaciation.
examples.cn: 上次冰期时冰盖覆盖了这片大陆。

dict_mnemonic.text: ice（冰）+ sheet（层、片）＝铺在大陆上的一层冰；比冰帽大、架在陆上、靠自身重量向外流，三个特征一起记。

root: 英语复合词，由 ice（冰，古英语 is）与 sheet（片、层，古英语 scete「一块布」）组合；地质义为 19 世纪所立。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of ice sheet. One continental body of ice produces the rest: its thickness, its area, its ancient forms, its balance, its edge, its record of air, and its counterparts on other planets.
sensesIntro.cn: ice sheet 的八个义项。一块大陆冰体衍生其余各义：厚度、面积、古代形态、质量平衡、边缘、封存的空气，以及其他行星上的对应物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick white layer spread over a whole continent, its edge slowly flowing outward.
core.cn: 核心意象：覆盖整块大陆的厚白层，边缘缓慢向外流动。

branches.en: THE BODY AND ITS FOOTPRINT: the ice mass, then the land it buries.
branches.cn: 冰体与其足迹：先是冰体，再是它掩埋的土地。

branches.en: MASS AND DEPTH: the same ice measured in kilometres.
branches.cn: 体量与厚度：以公里计的同一块冰。

branches.en: TIME AND BALANCE: an ancient sheet, then the accounting of gain and loss.
branches.cn: 时间与收支：先是一块古冰盖，再是增减的核算。

branches.en: EDGE AND ARCHIVE: where the ice meets the world, and what it keeps trapped inside.
branches.cn: 边缘与档案：冰与世界相接之处，以及它封存于内部的东西。

branches.en: ANOTHER PLANET: the same shape repeated at a Martian pole.
branches.cn: 另一颗行星：同一形状在火星极区重现。

intro.en: Ice sheet is a transparent compound of two free words, with no affix of its own; its technical force comes from the geological definition, not from morphology.
intro.cn: ice sheet 是两个自由词的透明复合，本身不带词缀；它的技术含义来自地质定义，而非构词。

latinIntro.en: Neither half has a Latin cognate: ice is Germanic and sheet is Germanic. Latin glacies also means ice, but it is a different root, not a relative; glacier and glacial belong to that other family.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都没有拉丁同族词：ice 与 sheet 都属日耳曼语。拉丁 glacies 也意为冰，但属另一词根，并非同源；glacier 与 glacial 属于那个词族。

items.example: Ice covered the bay.
A sheet of ice covered the lake.
The ice sheet is melting at its edges.
An ice cap covers the summit.

items.meaning: a mountain area of connected glaciers
items.meaningCN: 山区间相连冰川覆盖的区域
items.example: The ice field feeds many valleys.

items.meaning: a cylinder drilled from ice for study
items.meaningCN: 从冰中钻取用于研究的柱状样
items.example: The ice core records two thousand years.
items.exampleCN: 这根冰芯记录了两千年。

items.example: Ice sheets grew during the ice age.
The road was icy at dawn.

definition_zh: 指标；指示器；指示剂；指示物；转向灯
definition_en: something that shows a condition or points to a result, such as a gauge, a statistical measure or a warning light
core_image: 仪表盘上一根指针，把看不见的状态翻成看得见的刻度
scene: 这里指「指标」。 The unemployment rate is the most closely watched indicator of the economy's health.
sceneCN: 这里指第 1 个义项。这里 indicator 是「经济指标」（第 1、5 个义项：用来显示整体状况的可测量量）；句意：失业率是衡量经济健康最受关注的指标。图中可辨识物件：仪表盘、上升与下降的两条曲线、报摊上的报纸标题。

pos.zh: 指标；指示器；指示剂；指示物；转向灯

senses.title: A measurable sign of a condition
senses.definition: a statistic used to show the state or direction of a system
senses.definitionCN: 用来显示某系统状态或走向的统计量
senses.example: Inflation is a key indicator of economic stress.
senses.exampleCN: 通货膨胀是经济压力的关键指标。
senses.why: The suffix -or names the thing that does the pointing. An indicator is the finger itself, not the fact it aims at.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -or 命名做指向动作的事物。indicator 是手指本身，而不是它所指向的事实。

senses.title: A gauge or dial
senses.definition: a device that shows a reading such as pressure, speed or temperature
senses.definitionCN: 显示压力、速度或温度等读数的装置
senses.example: The temperature indicator warned of overheating.
senses.exampleCN: 温度指示器发出了过热警告。
senses.why: Here the pointing is mechanical. The needle converts an invisible quantity into a visible position on a scale.
senses.whyCN: 这里的指向是机械的。指针把不可见的量换算成刻度上的可见位置。

senses.title: A chemical that changes colour
senses.definition: in chemistry, a substance that changes colour to show a property such as acidity
senses.definitionCN: 化学中通过变色显示酸碱性等性质的物质
senses.example: Litmus is a classic pH indicator.
senses.exampleCN: 石蕊是一种经典的酸碱指示剂。
senses.why: The colour change is the pointing. The molecule raises a finger the moment a threshold is crossed.
senses.whyCN: 颜色变化就是那次指向。阈值一旦被越过，分子立刻举起一根手指。

senses.title: A species that reveals ecosystem health
senses.definition: in ecology, an organism whose condition reveals the health of its habitat
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中其状况能揭示栖息地健康的生物
senses.example: Lichens are useful indicators of air quality.
senses.exampleCN: 地衣是空气质量的实用指示物。
senses.why: A sensitive organism cannot help pointing. If it thrives, the habitat is well; if it dies, something is wrong.
senses.whyCN: 敏感的生物不由自主地指向。它繁盛，说明栖息地良好；它死亡，说明出了问题。

senses.title: An economic figure to watch
senses.definition: in economics, a published figure used to judge the direction of the economy
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中用来判断经济走向的公布数字
senses.example: Housing starts are a leading indicator of recovery.
senses.exampleCN: 新屋开工是复苏的先行指标。
senses.why: The metaphor becomes statistical: one number is chosen to stand for millions of unseen decisions.
senses.whyCN: 比喻变成统计性的：一个数字被选中，代表数百万个看不见的决策。

senses.title: A person who points something out
senses.definition: a person who indicates or draws attention to something
senses.definitionCN: 指出某事或引起注意的人
senses.example: He was the first indicator of the flaw in the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 他是最先指出计划缺陷的人。
senses.why: The rare human sense restores the literal finger: the indicator is a person doing the pointing.
senses.whyCN: 罕用的人称义恢复了字面手指：指示者就是一个在做指向动作的人。

senses.title: A car's flashing light
senses.definition: in British usage, the flashing light on a vehicle that shows the direction of a turn
senses.definitionCN: 英式用法中指车辆上显示转向方向的闪灯
senses.example: He forgot to use the indicator before turning.
senses.exampleCN: 他转弯前忘了打转向灯。
senses.why: The lamp points for the driver, announcing an intention before the vehicle moves. It is pointing made public.
senses.whyCN: 灯替驾驶员指出方向，在车辆移动之前宣布意图。这是公开化的指向。

senses.title: A warning sign of risk
senses.definition: an early sign that something may go wrong
senses.definitionCN: 某事可能出问题的早期信号
senses.example: A rise in complaints is an indicator of deeper trouble.
senses.exampleCN: 投诉上升是更深层问题的警示信号。
senses.why: The finger now points at the future. The sign is valuable because it appears before the damage.
senses.whyCN: 手指现在指向未来。信号之所以有价值，是因为它在损害出现之前就到了。

intro.en: Indicator is indicare plus -or, the suffix for the doer. It descends from Latin index, the pointer or forefinger, so the word is literally 'the one that points'. English first used it for people, then for gauges and figures.
intro.cn: indicator 是 indicare 加 -or，后者是表示施动者的后缀。它源自拉丁语 index“指示者、食指”，因此字面上就是“做指向的东西”。英语先把它用于人，后用于仪表与数字。

items.en: Dicare, 'to proclaim', shares a stem with dicere, 'to say'. The split between the two verbs is generally accepted but its exact prehistory is uncertain.
items.cn: dicare“宣告”与 dicere“说”共享词干。两个动词的分化一般被接受，但确切史前过程不确定。

items.en: Index meant 'one who points out, a sign, the forefinger'. It also named the list in a book, because a list points to pages.
items.cn: index 意为“指出者、标志、食指”。它也指书中的目录，因为目录指向页码。

items.en: Indicare meant 'to point out, to show'. Its agent noun indicator would have meant 'one who points out'; English built the noun fresh on the Latin stem.
items.cn: indicare 意为“指出、显示”。其施动名词 indicator 本应意为“指出者”；英语是在拉丁词干上重新造出这个名词。

items.en: The suffix -or forms agent nouns such as doctor and rector. Attached to indicare it gives 'the pointer', the thing or person that does the pointing.
items.cn: 后缀 -or 构成 doctor、rector 等施动名词。加在 indicare 上就得到“指向者”，即做指向的事物或人。

items.en: Early English indicators were people, especially informers or signallers. The instrument sense arrived with the growth of scientific instruments.
items.cn: 早期英语中的 indicator 指人，尤指告发者或信号员。仪器义随着科学仪器的增长而来。

items.en: Chemical indicators, engine gauges, ecological indicator species and economic leading indicators each put a different object in the pointing role.
items.cn: 化学指示剂、发动机仪表、生态指示物种与经济先行指标，各自把不同物件放在“指向者”的位置上。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the verb, the process noun and this agent noun. The meaning group compares words for measures and signals.
note.cn: 形近组区分动词、过程名词与这个施动名词；词义组比较表示测量与信号的词。

entries.definition: to point out or show. The indicator is the thing that performs this act.
entries.definitionCN: 指出或显示。indicator 是执行这一动作的事物。

entries.definition: a sign or the act of showing. It is the pointing, while indicator is the pointer.
entries.definitionCN: 迹象或显示的行为。它是指向，而 indicator 是指向者。

entries.definition: a list, a comparative number or the forefinger. It is the older Latin name for the same pointer.
entries.definitionCN: 清单、比较数字或食指。它是同一指向者的更早拉丁名称。

entries.definition: a quantity used to judge or compare. It is close to sense 01 but names the size, not the pointing function.
entries.definitionCN: 用于判断或比较的数量。它接近第 1 义项，但命名的是大小，而非指向功能。

entries.definition: a device for measuring. It is the physical object behind sense 02.
entries.definitionCN: 测量用的装置。它是第 2 义项背后的实物。

entries.definition: anything that suggests something else. It is broader than indicator and does not imply a designed measuring role.
entries.definitionCN: 暗示另一事物的任何东西。它比 indicator 更宽，不含被设计来测量的角色。

entries.definition: a gesture, sound or light that carries information. It matches sense 07 and stresses communication rather than measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 承载信息的手势、声音或光。它对应第 7 义项，强调传达而非测量。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build indicator from indicare plus -or and keep the image of a needle that turns an unseen quantity into a visible mark.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩从 indicare 加 -or 搭起 indicator，并保留“指针把看不见的量变成看得见的刻度”的意象。

normal.en: See -or: the one that points. An indicator does the pointing; an indication is what is pointed at.
normal.cn: 看见 -or：做指向的那一个。indicator 负责指，indication 是被指出的东西。

normal.en: Picture a dashboard needle: the engine's health becomes a position on a dial.
normal.cn: 想象仪表盘指针：发动机的健康变成一个表盘位置。

normal.en: In chemistry, the colour change is the needle.
normal.cn: 在化学里，颜色变化就是那根指针。

normal.en: A lichen is a living gauge for the air around it.
normal.cn: 地衣就是它周围空气的活仪表。

normal.en: Remember the chain: indicator points, indication appears, indicate is the act.
normal.cn: 记住这条链：indicator 指，indication 显现，indicate 是动作。

abstract.en: Keep one image: a small visible thing standing in for a large invisible one.
abstract.cn: 只记一个意象：一个小的可见之物，代表一个大的不可见之物。

abstract.en: Treat the word as a promise that the reading is connected to the reality it stands for.
abstract.cn: 把这个词当作一个承诺：读数与它所代表的事实是相连的。

abstract.en: Notice that an indicator can be wrong; that is why economists argue about which one to trust.
abstract.cn: 注意指标可能出错；正因如此，经济学家才争论该信哪一个。

examples.en: The report uses three indicators to rank the schools.
examples.cn: 这份报告用三项指标给学校排名。

examples.en: The indicator on the dashboard began to flash.
examples.cn: 仪表盘上的指示器开始闪动。

examples.en: Moss is a reliable indicator of damp conditions.
examples.cn: 苔藓是潮湿环境的可靠指示物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“印地开特”：在印度地图上开一个特别记号，一指就明白——指标、指示器。

root: 拉丁语 indicare“指出”（in- 朝向 + dicare 宣告）加施动后缀 -or；与 index“食指、索引”同源，字面义为“做指向的东西”。

sensesIntro.en: An indicator is the pointer, not the truth. It can be a statistic, a needle, a dye, a lichen, a leading economic figure, a person, a car lamp or an early warning. The eight senses differ in material and in what is being pointed at, but each one converts something hard to see into something that can be read.
sensesIntro.cn: indicator 是指向者，而不是真相。它可以是统计数字、指针、染料、地衣、经济先行数据、一个人、一盏车灯或一次预警。八个义项的差别在材质与所指对象，但每一个都把难以看见的东西变成可读的东西。

core.en: A pointer that makes an unseen condition readable.
core.cn: 使看不见的状况变得可读的指向者。

branches.en: NUMBERS: statistics that stand for a whole system.
branches.cn: 数字：代表整个系统的统计量。

branches.en: DEVICES: needles and lamps that show a state or an intention.
branches.cn: 装置：显示状态或意图的指针与灯。

branches.en: NATURE: dyes and organisms that react before we can measure.
branches.cn: 自然：在我们能测量之前就反应的染料与生物。

branches.en: PERSON: someone who points a problem out.
branches.cn: 人：指出问题的人。

branches.en: WARNING: a sign that arrives before the damage.
branches.cn: 警示：在损害之前到达的信号。

intro.en: Indicator is indicare plus -or. The items below show the agent suffix at work and the pointing family around it.
intro.cn: indicator 是 indicare 加 -or。下列条目展示施动后缀的作用，以及它周围的“指向”词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the pointing noun, the verb and the verb's root. They explain why a forefinger, an index and an indicator are one family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出指向名词、动词及其词根。它们解释了为什么食指、索引与指标是一个家族。

items.meaning: a thing or person that points out
items.example: The indicator fell below zero.
The map indicates where the river once ran.
items.exampleCN: 地图标示出这条河曾经的走向。

items.example: There is little indication of change.
The vote is indicative of public anger.
items.exampleCN: 这次投票显示了公众的愤怒。

items.meaning: a list or a comparative number
items.example: The index tracks housing costs.
Two indices showed the same trend.
items.exampleCN: 两个指数显示出同一趋势。

items.meaning: a plant that reveals soil conditions
items.example: The indicator-plant thrived on copper-rich soil.
items.exampleCN: 这种指示植物在富铜土壤上长得很好。

items.meaning: as a sign rather than as proof
items.example: The figures are indicatively useful.
items.exampleCN: 这些数字具有提示性的用处。

definition_zh: 引力的；重力的；万有引力的；由引力造成的
definition_en: relating to the force by which masses attract one another, or produced by that force
core_image: 一颗小球沿弯曲的网格面滚向中央的大球
scene: 这里指「引力的」。 The satellite stays in orbit because gravitational attraction balances its speed.
sceneCN: 这里 gravitational 是「引力的」（第 1 个义项：与质量相互吸引的力有关）；句意：卫星之所以留在轨道上，是因为引力吸引与它的速度相平衡。图中可辨识物件：弯曲的网格面、中央大球、环绕小卫星、轨道线、速度箭头。

pos.zh: 引力的；重力的；万有引力的（多作定语）

derivatives.zh: 引力子（假设的引力传播粒子）

senses.title: Of the force between masses
senses.titleCN: 引力的：质量之间相互吸引的
senses.definition: relating to the attraction that any two bodies with mass exert on each other
senses.definitionCN: 关于任何两个有质量的物体相互施加的吸引
senses.example: The two stars are locked in a gravitational embrace.
senses.exampleCN: 这两颗恒星被引力的拥抱锁定在一起。
senses.why: gravitation comes from Latin gravitas 'heaviness'; -al makes the adjective, so gravitational marks whatever belongs to that heaviness-driven attraction.
senses.whyCN: gravitation 出自拉丁 gravitas“沉重”；-al 构成形容词，因此 gravitational 标记属于这种由“重”驱动的吸引的事物。

senses.title: Of Newton's universal law
senses.titleCN: 万有引力定律的：平方反比的那条规律
senses.definition: relating to the law stating that attraction grows with mass and falls with the square of distance
senses.definitionCN: 关于“引力随质量增大、随距离平方减小”这一定律的
senses.example: The spacecraft's path was computed with the gravitational law alone.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘飞船的轨迹仅用万有引力定律就算了出来。
senses.why: Newton's law turned everyday falling into a single rule for all bodies, so the adjective acquired this precise law-based sense.
senses.whyCN: 牛顿定律把日常下落变成适用于一切物体的单一规律，这个形容词于是获得这一精确的“定律”义。

senses.title: Caused by attraction
senses.titleCN: 由引力造成的：潮汐与落体
senses.definition: produced by gravitational attraction, as in tides or a falling stone
senses.definitionCN: 由引力吸引造成的，如潮汐或落石
senses.example: Tidal motion is a gravitational effect of the moon on the ocean.
senses.exampleCN: 潮汐运动是月球对海洋产生的引力效应。
senses.why: Once the force is named, its visible results can be labelled with the adjective: the tide is water answering the moon's pull.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这种力被命名，其可见结果就可用该形容词标记：潮汐就是海水对月球牵引的回应。

senses.title: Of ripples in spacetime
senses.definition: relating to waves in spacetime produced by accelerating massive bodies
senses.definitionCN: 关于加速运动的大质量天体在时空中产生的波
senses.example: The detector recorded a gravitational wave from two merging black holes.
senses.exampleCN: 探测器记录到来自两个并合黑洞的引力波。
senses.why: General relativity recast gravity as curvature, and a changing curvature travels as a wave; the adjective simply follows that new object.
senses.whyCN: 广义相对论把引力重述为时空弯曲，而变化的弯曲会以波的形式传播；这个形容词便随之指向这一新对象。

senses.title: Of the field around a mass
senses.titleCN: 引力场的：质量周围的作用区域
senses.definition: relating to the region in which a mass exerts attraction on other bodies
senses.definitionCN: 关于某质量对其他物体施加吸引的作用区域
senses.example: Inside the gravitational field of the planet, every path bends.
senses.exampleCN: 在这颗行星的引力场中，每条路径都会弯曲。
senses.why: Physicists describe action at a distance as a field filling space, so the adjective attaches to that region rather than to the force itself.
senses.whyCN: 物理学家把超距作用描述为充满空间的场，因此这个形容词附着于那一区域，而非力的本身。

senses.title: Of bent light
senses.titleCN: 引力透镜的：光被质量折弯
senses.definition: relating to the bending of light by a massive object, which can magnify images behind it
senses.definitionCN: 关于大质量天体使光弯折、从而放大其后方图像的
senses.example: A gravitational lens made the distant galaxy appear as a ring.
senses.exampleCN: 一个引力透镜使那个遥远星系呈现为环状。
senses.why: If mass curves space, light crossing that curve is bent like a ray through glass; astronomers borrowed the lens metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 若质量使空间弯曲，穿过该弯曲的光就像经过玻璃的光线一样被折弯；天文学家借用了透镜的比喻。

senses.title: Irresistibly attractive
senses.titleCN: 比喻：具有强大吸引力的
senses.definition: used figuratively of a strong pull that draws people, money or attention
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指把人、资金或注意力吸过去的强大牵引
senses.example: The city has a gravitational pull for graduates from the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市对整个地区的毕业生都有一种引力般的吸引力。
senses.why: The literal force pulls matter without contact; economics and sociology borrow it for any centre that draws things in.
senses.whyCN: 这一字面之力不接触就把物质拉过去；经济学与社会学便借它指任何把事物吸向自己的中心。

senses.title: Of weight and stored energy
senses.titleCN: 重力作用的：重量与势能
senses.definition: relating to the effect of weight, as in potential energy or the load on a structure
senses.definitionCN: 关于重量效应的，如势能或结构所受的荷载
senses.example: The dam converts gravitational potential energy into electricity.
senses.exampleCN: 水坝把重力势能转化为电能。
senses.why: In engineering the same force appears as a load or a store of energy, and the adjective names that practical face.
senses.whyCN: 在工程中，同一股力表现为荷载或能量储存，这个形容词命名的正是它的实用面。

intro.en: Gravitational is gravitation plus -al, built on Latin gravitas 'heaviness' from gravis 'heavy'. The physics sense dates from the Newtonian period. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: gravitational 是 gravitation 加 -al，词基为拉丁 gravitas“沉重”，出自 gravis“重的”。物理义形成于牛顿时代。年代为约数。

items.en: gravis meant 'heavy, weighty, serious'. Its noun gravitas covered physical weight and personal dignity at once, a pairing that still survives in English gravity.
items.cn: gravis 意为“重的、有分量的、严肃的”。其名词 gravitas 同时覆盖物理重量与个人威严，这一配对在英语 gravity 中仍然保留。

items.en: Late Latin formed gravitatio 'a weighing down', from the verb gravitare. The modern physical sense was read into this pattern much later.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁由动词 gravitare 构成 gravitatio“压下去、加重”。现代物理义是后来才被读入这一构词模式的。

items.en: English gravitation is recorded in the 17th century, and Newton's Principia of 1687 gave the word its lasting meaning: mutual attraction between all masses.
items.cn: 英语 gravitation 于 17 世纪有记录；1687 年牛顿的《原理》赋予该词持久含义：一切质量之间的相互吸引。

items.en: gravitational is the relational adjective, formed with -al from the noun. It appears later than gravitation and spreads with technical writing.
items.cn: gravitational 是由名词加 -al 构成的关系形容词，出现晚于 gravitation，并随技术写作而传播。

items.en: After 1915 general relativity added gravitational waves, gravitational lensing and gravitational fields to the adjective's range.
items.cn: 1915 年之后，广义相对论为这个形容词增添了引力波、引力透镜与引力场等用法。

items.en: The exact date of the first English use of gravitational is uncertain, and the deeper Indo-European source of gravis is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: gravitational 在英语中的确切首用年代存疑；gravis 的更深印欧来源属重构而非有据。

note.en: The first group contains forms from the same root that are easily confused; the second contains related physical and figurative adjectives.
note.cn: 第一组是同根易混形式；第二组是相关的物理与比喻形容词。

entries.definition: The process or force of attraction itself. It names the phenomenon; gravitational describes something belonging to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指吸引过程或力本身，命名的是现象；gravitational 描述属于该现象的事物。

entries.definition: The force, especially near a planet, and also seriousness of manner or situation. It is broader than the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指力，尤指行星附近的力，也指举止或情势的严肃；比该形容词更宽。

entries.definition: To move under gravity, or to be drawn towards something. It is the action form, not the attribute.
entries.definitionCN: 在重力下移动，或被某物吸引；是动作形式，而非属性。

entries.definition: As an adjective, 'serious'; as a noun, 'a burial place' from a different Old English word. Only the adjective shares gravis.
entries.definitionCN: 作形容词意为“严重的”，作名词指“坟墓”且出自另一古英语词；只有形容词与 gravis 同源。

entries.definition: Relating to magnetism, which attracts only certain materials and can repel; gravity attracts all mass and never repels.
entries.definitionCN: 关于磁力，只吸引某些材料且可排斥；引力吸引一切质量且从不排斥。

entries.definition: Directed towards a centre, describing the motion of a body in a curved path; gravity often supplies it.
entries.definitionCN: 指向中心，描述物体沿曲线路径的运动；常由引力提供。

entries.definition: Relating to an orbit, the path itself rather than the attraction that shapes it.
entries.definitionCN: 关于轨道的，指路径本身，而非塑造路径的吸引。

entries.definition: Relating to tides, one visible gravitational effect rather than the force in general.
entries.definitionCN: 关于潮汐的，指一种可见的引力效应，而非力本身。

entries.definition: Heavy in weight or serious in importance; it shares the figurative 'heaviness' of gravity but is not a physics term.
entries.definitionCN: 指重量大或重要性高；与 gravity 共享比喻性的“重”，但不是物理术语。

normal.cn: 同族词是 gravitation、gravitational、gravity、gravitate、graviton。

normal.en: The word keeps Latin gravis 'heavy' inside it, which links it to grave and gravity.
normal.cn: 这个词内部保留着拉丁 gravis“重”，因此与 grave、gravity 相连。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy ball sinking into a stretched sheet while small marbles curve around it.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗重球压陷一张绷紧的膜，小弹珠绕着它弯曲滚动。

abstract.en: Picture light from a distant galaxy bending around a cluster and arriving as a ring.
abstract.cn: 想象来自遥远星系的光绕过星系团弯折，最终以环状抵达。

abstract.en: Picture a city drawing graduates inward as if it had its own weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市像自带重量一样把毕业生吸向中心。

examples.en: The probe measured gravitational variations that revealed a buried crater.
examples.cn: 探测器测得的引力变化揭示了一个被埋藏的陨石坑。

examples.en: Two neutron stars spiralled inward, radiating gravitational waves.
examples.cn: 两颗中子星盘旋靠近，辐射出引力波。

examples.en: The region's gravitational pull on young workers worries smaller towns.
examples.cn: 该地区对年轻劳动者的吸引力令小城镇担忧。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one physical image, a mass bending the space around it, and then extend that pull into waves, fields, bent light and even economics.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一个物理意象展开：一个质量使周围空间弯曲；随后这股牵引被延伸到波、场、被折弯的光，乃至经济。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small ball rolling down a curved grid towards a heavy centre.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗小球沿弯曲的网格滚向沉重的中心。

branches.en: THE FORCE AND ITS LAW: the general attraction and Newton's precise rule are one idea at two levels of exactness.
branches.cn: 力与定律：一般吸引与牛顿的精确规律是同一想法在两个精确程度上。

branches.en: VISIBLE EFFECTS: tides, falling stones and stored potential energy are the force made observable.
branches.cn: 可见效应：潮汐、落石与储存的势能，是这股力变得可观察。

branches.en: RELATIVITY: waves and fields recast attraction as geometry that fills and ripples through space.
branches.cn: 相对论：波与场把吸引重述为充满空间并产生涟漪的几何。

branches.en: BENT LIGHT: if space curves, light must curve, and a mass becomes a lens.
branches.cn: 弯折的光：若空间弯曲，光必然弯曲，于是质量成了透镜。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE PULL: any centre that draws people or money borrows the physics.
branches.cn: 比喻性的牵引：任何吸走人或资金的中心都借用了这套物理。

intro.en: Gravitational is built from the Latin root grav- 'heavy', the noun-forming -itatio and the adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: gravitational 由拉丁词根 grav-“重”、名词构成成分 -itatio 与形容词词尾 -al 组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin gravis and gravitas produced a small English family: gravity, grave, gravitate, gravitation, gravitational and the modern coined graviton.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 gravis 与 gravitas 产出一个小型英语词族：gravity、grave、gravitate、gravitation、gravitational，以及现代新造的 graviton。

items.example: The gravitational field is strongest near the surface.
items.exampleCN: 引力场在地表附近最强。

items.meaning: the process of attraction between masses

definition_zh: 哀叹；悲叹；抱怨；惋惜
definition_en: to express sadness or dissatisfaction about something, often again and again
core_image: 深夜坐在窗边、对着旧照片一声接一声地叹气
scene: 老人抚摸着泛黄的合影，一遍遍叹气。 The old man bemoaned the loss of the quiet village of his childhood.
