definition_zh: 沙尘暴；沙暴
definition_en: a strong wind that carries sand and dust through the air
core_image: 一堵黄褐色的沙墙从地平线推过来，把天空和太阳一起吞掉
scene: 午后远处地平线升起一堵黄褐色的墙，几分钟内把太阳吞掉。 A sandstorm turned noon into dusk and forced the convoy to stop.
sceneCN: 这里 sandstorm 指「沙尘暴」（第 1 个义项：强风把大量沙尘卷起、遮蔽天空的天气现象）；句意为沙尘暴把正午变成黄昏，车队被迫停下。

pos.zh: 沙尘暴；沙暴（可数，复数 sandstorms）

derivatives.zh: sand（复合词前项，古英语 sand，无后缀）→ 沙
sand + -y（古英语 -ig，形容词后缀）→ 多沙的；引申为沙色的
storm（复合词后项，古英语 storm，无后缀）→ 风暴；暴风雨
storm + -y（古英语 -ig，形容词后缀）→ 有风暴的；引申为激烈的
dust + storm（复合术语，无后缀）→ 以细尘为主的风暴：尘暴

senses.title: A wind-borne wall of sand
senses.definition: a strong wind carrying large amounts of sand and dust, reducing visibility
senses.definitionCN: 强风携带大量沙尘、降低能见度的天气现象
senses.example: A sandstorm turned noon into dusk and forced the convoy to stop.
senses.exampleCN: 沙尘暴把正午变成黄昏，车队被迫停下。
senses.why: sand and storm are placed side by side: the word names a storm whose visible load is sand.
senses.whyCN: sand 与 storm 直接并置：这个词命名一场可见负荷为沙的风暴。

senses.title: A sand-dominated wind
senses.titleCN: 沙暴：以沙粒为主的强风
senses.definition: a wind event dominated by coarse sand rather than fine dust
senses.definitionCN: 以粗沙粒而非细尘为主的强风事件
senses.example: The sandstorm stripped paint from the cars.
senses.exampleCN: 沙暴把车漆打磨掉了。
senses.why: meteorology separates coarse sand from fine dust, so the same event has a sand-dominated reading.
senses.whyCN: 气象学把粗沙与细尘分开，因此同一事件有「以沙为主」的读法。

senses.title: The sand and dust it leaves
senses.titleCN: 落尘：沙尘暴留下的沙土
senses.definition: the sand and dust deposited after a sandstorm passes
senses.definitionCN: 沙尘暴过后落下的沙与尘
senses.example: The sandstorm left a layer of dust on every window.
senses.exampleCN: 沙尘暴在每扇窗上留下一层尘土。
senses.why: the storm deposits what it carries, so the word names the material left behind as well as the event.
senses.whyCN: 风暴卸下它所携带之物，因此这个词既命名事件，也命名留下的材料。

senses.title: A single storm event
senses.titleCN: 一次沙暴事件：可计数的一场
senses.definition: one occurrence of such a storm, countable in weather records
senses.definitionCN: 此类风暴的一次发生，在气象记录中可计数
senses.example: The region records dozens of sandstorms a year.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区每年记录数十次沙尘暴。
senses.why: weather records count events, so the mass noun acquires a countable sense.
senses.whyCN: 气象记录要计数事件，因此这个物质名词获得可数义。

senses.title: A sand source area
senses.titleCN: 沙源地：沙尘暴的物质来源
senses.definition: a dry area, such as a lake bed or desert, that supplies sand to storms
senses.definitionCN: 干涸湖床或沙漠等向风暴提供沙尘的地区
senses.example: Dry lake beds are major sandstorm sources.
senses.exampleCN: 干涸湖床是主要的沙尘暴源地。
senses.why: every storm starts somewhere dry, so the word names the source area as well as the event.
senses.whyCN: 每场沙尘暴都起于某处干旱地面，因此这个词既命名事件，也命名源地。

senses.title: A sandstorm warning
senses.definition: an official alert issued when a sandstorm is expected
senses.definitionCN: 预计出现沙尘暴时发布的官方警报
senses.example: Forecasters issued a sandstorm warning for the afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 预报员发布了下午的沙尘暴预警。
senses.why: forecasting turns the event into an alert, so the word names the official warning.
senses.whyCN: 预报把事件变成警报，因此这个词命名官方预警。

senses.title: The impacts of a sandstorm
senses.titleCN: 沙尘暴影响：能见度、交通与健康
senses.definition: the effects of a sandstorm on visibility, transport, health and equipment
senses.definitionCN: 沙尘暴对能见度、交通、健康与设备的影响
senses.example: Visibility fell to zero during the sandstorm.
senses.exampleCN: 沙尘暴期间能见度降为零。
senses.why: the event is also defined by its effects, so the word names impacts on visibility, transport and health.
senses.whyCN: 事件也由其影响界定，因此这个词命名对能见度、交通与健康的影响。

senses.title: An overwhelming surge
senses.titleCN: 比喻：铺天盖地、令人窒息的冲击
senses.definition: a sudden overwhelming quantity of something that feels like a storm of sand
senses.definitionCN: 突然铺天盖地、像沙暴一样令人窒息的量
senses.example: The office faced a sandstorm of complaints.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室面对铺天盖地的投诉。
senses.why: the shape of a wall of sand is transferred to any overwhelming surge, giving the metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 沙墙的形状被移到任何铺天盖地的冲击上，形成比喻。

intro.en: Sandstorm is a native English compound of sand and storm. Sand goes back to Old English sand, and storm to Old English storm. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sandstorm 是英语本族复合词，由 sand 与 storm 构成。sand 上承古英语 sand，storm 上承古英语 storm。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sand is the Germanic word for granular rock, with German Sand as a close relative.
items.cn: sand 是日耳曼语的颗粒岩石词，德语 Sand 是近亲。

items.en: Storm meant a tempest or violent weather; its deeper Germanic connections are reconstructed rather than certain.
items.cn: storm 指暴风雨或剧烈天气；其更早的日耳曼语联系属重构而非确定。

items.en: Sand plus storm appears in eighteenth- and nineteenth-century travel writing about deserts and dry plains.
items.cn: sand 加 storm 见于 18 与 19 世纪关于沙漠与干旱平原的游记。

items.en: Twentieth-century meteorology separates sandstorm from dust storm by particle size and height, and names regional types such as the haboob.
items.cn: 20 世纪气象学按颗粒大小与高度区分沙尘暴与尘暴，并命名哈布沙暴等区域类型。

items.en: Recent usage links sandstorms to desertification, air quality and respiratory health.
items.cn: 近期用法把沙尘暴与荒漠化、空气质量及呼吸健康联系起来。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the parts are securely documented, but the compound's first citation is dated differently in different sources.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：两个成分均有可靠记载，但复合词的最早书证各家年代不一。

note.en: Group one holds the sand compounds most easily mistaken for sandstorm; group two holds the other wind-and-dust weather terms.
note.cn: 第一组是最易被误认成 sandstorm 的 sand 复合词；第二组是其他风沙天气术语。

entries.definition: Loose granular rock; a sandstorm is that material in violent motion.
entries.definitionCN: 松散的颗粒岩石；沙尘暴是它在剧烈运动中的状态。

entries.definition: Rock made of cemented sand grains; it is solid and has nothing to do with weather.
entries.definitionCN: 由胶结沙粒构成的岩石；它是固体，与天气无关。

entries.definition: Sand saturated with water that cannot support weight; it is still, not blown.
entries.definitionCN: 饱含水的沙，无法承重；它静止不动，不被风吹。

entries.definition: A ridge of sand built in water by currents or waves, not by a storm in the air.
entries.definitionCN: 水流或波浪在水中堆成的沙脊，不是空中风暴所造。

entries.definition: A storm carrying fine dust over a wider area, often higher in the air than a sandstorm.
entries.definitionCN: 携带细尘、范围更广的风暴，尘常被扬得比沙尘暴更高。

entries.definition: A violent sand or dust storm of the Sudan and Arabian regions, often forming a dense wall.
entries.definitionCN: 苏丹与阿拉伯地区的强沙尘暴，常形成致密沙墙。

entries.definition: A severe snowstorm with strong wind and low visibility; the same structure, a different load.
entries.definitionCN: 强风低能见度的暴雪；结构相同，负荷不同。

entries.definition: A hot, dusty wind from North Africa reaching the Mediterranean; the wind itself, not the storm.
entries.definitionCN: 从北非吹到地中海的干热多尘风；指风本身，而非风暴。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds and real neighbours, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合词与邻近术语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sand + storm: a storm whose cargo is sand.
normal.cn: sand + storm：货物是沙的风暴。

normal.en: Sandstorm is coarse and low; dust storm is fine and high.
normal.cn: 沙尘暴颗粒粗、位置低；尘暴颗粒细、扬得高。

normal.en: Blizzard is the same structure with snow; once you see the pattern, the words explain themselves.
normal.cn: blizzard 是同一结构换成雪；看懂模式，词就自我解释。

normal.en: A sandstorm warning is about visibility; a sandstorm source is about where the sand starts.
normal.cn: 沙尘暴预警关注能见度，沙源地关注沙从哪里起。

normal.en: Dry lake beds and deserts are the two classic sandstorm sources.
normal.cn: 干涸湖床与沙漠是两类典型的沙尘暴源地。

abstract.en: A sandstorm is a landscape that decides to travel.
abstract.cn: 沙尘暴是一块决定出行的景观。

abstract.en: A storm of complaints can bury a project as fast as any wall of sand.
abstract.cn: 投诉的风暴能像沙墙一样迅速埋掉一个项目。

abstract.en: The dust a sandstorm leaves is geography arriving at your window.
abstract.cn: 沙尘暴留下的尘土，是地理来到你的窗前。

examples.en: A sandstorm closed the airport for two days.
examples.cn: 沙尘暴使机场关闭了两天。

examples.en: Drivers were warned about the sandstorm on the highway.
examples.cn: 司机们收到高速公路上沙尘暴的警告。

examples.en: The sandstorm stripped the paint from the signs.
examples.cn: 沙尘暴剥掉了标牌上的漆。

dict_mnemonic.text: sand（沙）+ storm（风暴）＝以沙为负荷的风暴；与 dust storm（细尘）、blizzard（雪）、haboob（区域型）对照记忆。

root: 英语本族复合词，由 sand（沙，古英语 sand）与 storm（风暴，古英语 storm）组合。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of sandstorm. The weather event yields the sand it leaves, a countable occurrence, its source, its warning, its impacts, and finally any overwhelming surge.
sensesIntro.cn: sandstorm 的八个义项。天气事件衍生出落尘、可计数的一次事件、源地、预警、影响，最后是任何铺天盖地的冲击。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brown wall of sand moves across the horizon and swallows the sun.
core.cn: 核心意象：一堵褐色沙墙越过地平线，把太阳吞掉。

branches.en: THE EVENT AND ITS LOAD: the storm as weather, then its coarse sand.
branches.cn: 事件与负荷：先是作为天气的风暴，再是其粗沙。

branches.en: WHAT IT LEAVES AND HOW OFTEN: deposited dust, then one countable occurrence.
branches.cn: 留下什么与发生几次：先是被落下的尘土，再是可计数的一次。

branches.en: WHERE IT BEGINS AND HOW IT IS ANNOUNCED: the source area, then the official warning.
branches.cn: 从何处起与如何预告：先是源地，再是官方预警。

branches.en: WHAT IT DOES: visibility, transport, health and equipment.
branches.cn: 它造成什么：能见度、交通、健康与设备。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: any sudden overwhelming quantity.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何突然铺天盖地的量。

intro.en: Sandstorm is a bare compound of two free words. English adds only the plural -s; the interpretive work is done by the two nouns.
intro.cn: sandstorm 是两个自由词的直接复合。英语只加复数 -s；解释工作由两个名词完成。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are Germanic and have no Latin cognates. Latin arena means sand but is unrelated, and tempestas means storm but is likewise unrelated.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词。拉丁 arena 意为沙、tempestas 意为风暴，但都与它不同源。

items.example: Sand filled the road.
The storm broke at noon.
A sandstorm hit the camp.
Spring brings frequent sandstorms.
items.exampleCN: 春天带来频繁的沙尘暴。

items.example: The soil is sandy and drains fast.
The crossing was stormy.
A dust storm reduced visibility across the plain.
items.exampleCN: 尘暴降低了平原上的能见度。

items.meaning: to clean or cut a surface with sand driven by air
items.meaningCN: 用气流喷沙清理或切割表面
items.example: They sandblasted the old paint away.
items.exampleCN: 他们用喷沙把旧漆打掉。

definition_zh: 表明；预示；是……的迹象（用间接线索指出某种情况存在或将要发生，本身不下定论）
definition_en: to be a sign that something exists or is likely to happen, pointing at it without stating it as proved
core_image: 医生在化验单上圈出一行偏高的数值，数值本身不说话，却指向体内还没退去的感染
scene: 查房时医生指着化验单上一行偏高的数值，说这往往提示体内还有没退去的感染。 A raised white cell count can be indicative of an infection that has not yet cleared.
sceneCN: 这里指化验数值作为间接线索指出感染仍在（第 1 个义项：作为迹象表明某事物存在）；句意为白细胞计数偏高可能提示感染尚未清除。图中可辨识物件：化验单、红笔圈出的数值、病床。

pos.zh: （固定搭配）表明；预示；是……的迹象

collocations.phrase: be indicative of the fact that

derivatives.zh: 由同一拉丁动词而来，义为「指出、表明」
由动词加表示结果的名词尾构成，义为「迹象、指示」
由动词加表示工具或施动者的名词尾构成，义为「指标」
由形容词加副词尾构成，义为「指示性地」
与「指出」同出拉丁语，本义「指点者」，义为「索引、指数」

senses.title: A sign that something exists
senses.titleCN: 作为迹象表明某事物存在
senses.definition: to point at something present which has not been directly observed
senses.definitionCN: 指用可以观察到的线索指出某事物确实存在，而该事物本身没有被直接看到
senses.example: Moss along the north wall can be indicative of constant damp in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 北墙根部的青苔可能表明这个房间长期潮湿。
senses.why: The adjective marks a pointer rather than a proof, so the phrase stops one step short of a claim.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只标出「指向」，不表示「证明」，所以整个短语比断言少走一步。

senses.title: A forecast of what is coming
senses.definition: to suggest that a future change is already under way
senses.definitionCN: 指某种迹象显示将来的变化已经开始露头
senses.example: A sudden fall in orders can be indicative of a slowdown later in the year.
senses.exampleCN: 订单突然下滑可能预示年内稍晚会出现放缓。
senses.why: A pointer can aim forward as easily as at the present, and the future sense grew out of the same gesture.
senses.whyCN: 指向的动作既可朝前也可朝当下，将来义就是从同一个手势里长出来的。

senses.title: A pattern read from data
senses.definition: to show, through figures or records, that a wider pattern is present
senses.definitionCN: 指通过数字或记录显示某种更大范围的规律确实存在
senses.example: The spread of test scores can be indicative of how uneven the teaching has been.
senses.exampleCN: 分数的分布情况可能反映出教学水平的参差。
senses.why: Numbers are pointers on paper, which is why this sense dominates reports and surveys.
senses.whyCN: 数字是纸上的指点标记，所以这个义项在报告与调查里最常见。

senses.title: A clinical hint
senses.definition: to suggest a medical condition before it has been confirmed
senses.definitionCN: 指在确诊之前提示可能存在某种疾病
senses.example: Persistent thirst can be indicative of a problem with blood sugar.
senses.exampleCN: 持续口渴可能提示血糖方面存在问题。
senses.why: Medicine is the place where a sign is most carefully separated from a diagnosis.
senses.whyCN: 医学是最讲究把「迹象」与「诊断」分开的地方。

senses.title: Evidence about the distant past
senses.definition: to point at conditions that no longer exist, through what they left behind
senses.definitionCN: 指通过遗留下来的痕迹指出如今已不存在的环境条件
senses.example: Shells in this layer can be indicative of a shallow sea that once covered the plain.
senses.exampleCN: 这一层里的贝壳可能表明这片平原过去曾是浅海。
senses.why: What remains is only a trace, so the phrase suits fields that must reason from traces.
senses.whyCN: 留存下来的只是痕迹，所以这个短语特别适合必须从痕迹推断的学科。

senses.title: A hedged claim in academic writing
senses.titleCN: 学术写作中的留有余地
senses.definition: to mark an inference as probable while keeping it open to revision
senses.definitionCN: 指把推断标成「可能」而保留被修正的余地
senses.example: The early results can be indicative of a wider effect, although the sample is small.
senses.exampleCN: 早期结果可能提示存在更广泛的影响，尽管样本很小。
senses.why: Scholars use the phrase because it lets a pointer stand in for a conclusion without claiming one.
senses.whyCN: 学者爱用它，是因为它让「指向」代替结论，却不必真的下结论。

senses.title: A marker of shared values
senses.definition: to stand as an outward sign of an attitude or value held by a group
senses.definitionCN: 指以外在可见的做法显示某个群体持有的态度或价值
senses.example: The way a town treats its old buildings can be indicative of what it values.
senses.exampleCN: 一个小镇对待老建筑的方式，可能表明它看重什么。
senses.why: The pointer here aims at something invisible, so habits become the visible sign of it.
senses.whyCN: 这里的指向对着看不见的东西，于是日常做法成了它的可见标记。

senses.title: A clue that falls short of proof
senses.definition: to raise a suspicion that still needs confirmation from another source
senses.definitionCN: 指提出一个仍须由其他来源加以确认的怀疑
senses.example: A single late record can be indicative of a problem, but it cannot prove one.
senses.exampleCN: 单独一次迟到记录可能提示问题，却无法证明问题存在。
senses.why: The phrase keeps its force by staying short of proof, which is exactly its value in argument.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语的力量正来自「不到证明」，这也正是它在论证中的价值。

intro.en: Indicative comes from Latin indicativus, from indicare, to point out, built on in- and dicare, to proclaim. English borrowed the adjective in the sixteenth century as a grammar term, and the frame be indicative of is a native English pattern whose first date is uncertain.
intro.cn: indicative 出自拉丁语 indicativus，而后者来自 indicare「指出」，由 in- 与 dicare「宣告」构成。英语十六世纪先把它当作语法术语借入，而「be indicative of」是英语本土的「系动词加形容词加介词」框架，首见年代不确定。

items.en: Dicare meant to proclaim or make known, and it is a cousin rather than a twin of dicere, to say.
items.cn: dicare 意为宣告、使人知道，它与 dicere「说」是近亲而非同一个词。

items.en: In- plus dicare produced indicare, to point out or show, the verb that stands behind the whole family.
items.cn: in- 与 dicare 合成 indicare，意为指出、显示，是整个词族的动词源头。

items.en: The adjective indicativus named the mood that states facts, and English took it over as indicative.
items.cn: 形容词 indicativus 用来命名陈述事实的语气，英语照此借入 indicative。

items.en: Indicative entered English first as a grammar label before it spread into general description.
items.cn: indicative 先以语法标签的身份进入英语，之后才扩展到一般描述。

items.en: The pattern be + adjective + of is inherited English grammar, so the phrase is a construction rather than a borrowed unit; its first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 「系动词加形容词加 of」是英语继承下来的语法框架，所以这个短语是构造出来的而非整体借入，首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the pointing verb or the same adjective; the second group names neighbouring ways of hinting.
note.cn: 第一组共享「指出」这个动词或同一个形容词；第二组是与「暗示」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to point out or show directly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，指直接指出或显示。

entries.definition: A sign or piece of evidence pointing at something.
entries.definitionCN: 指指向某事物的迹象或证据。

entries.definition: A measurable quantity used to read a condition.
entries.definitionCN: 指用来判断状况的可测指标。

entries.definition: A pointer, list or ratio, from the same 'point out' verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指索引、指针或指数，同出「指出」一词。

entries.definition: The clause variant, which takes a full statement instead of a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 从句变体，后面接完整陈述而不是名词。

entries.definition: To hint at something without stating it, usually weaker than a proof.
entries.definitionCN: 指不点明地暗示，通常比证据弱。

entries.definition: To call something to mind as a likely explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 指让人联想到某种可能的解释。

entries.definition: To indicate a likely cause or answer.
entries.definitionCN: 指指向可能的原因或答案。

entries.definition: To show that something is happening or about to happen.
entries.definitionCN: 指显示某事正在或即将发生。

entries.definition: The plainest way to say that one thing marks another.
entries.definitionCN: 是最平实的说法，表示一物是另一物的标志。

entries.definition: To leave something to be understood rather than said.
entries.definitionCN: 指把意思留给对方领会而不明说。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the 'proclaim' root inside indicate, the adjective-plus-of frame, and the clinic where the phrase is most often heard.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用「宣告」这个词根记住这个动词，用「形容词加介词」的框架记住搭配，再借最常听到它的诊室场景固定下来。

normal.en: Dicare means to proclaim, so indicate is to point something out for others to see.
normal.cn: dicare 是「宣告」，所以 indicate 就是把某物指出来给别人看。

normal.en: The adjective plus of frame puts the pointed-at object right after the preposition.
normal.cn: 形容词加 of 的框架，把被指的对象直接放在介词后面。

normal.en: Suggest is its soft neighbour, but suggest can stand alone while this phrase needs a noun after of.
normal.cn: suggest 是它语气柔和的邻居，但 suggest 可以单独用，这个短语的 of 后面必须接名词。

normal.en: Hospital reports love the phrase because a number can hint without diagnosing.
normal.cn: 医院报告爱用它，因为一个数值可以提示却不等于诊断。

normal.en: For a clause, swap the phrase for be indicative that and keep the same meaning.
normal.cn: 要接从句时，把短语换成「be indicative that」，意思不变。

abstract.en: A sign is a road sign: it points the way but does not walk it for you.
abstract.cn: 迹象像路标，指向方向却不替你走路。

abstract.en: How a society treats its oldest buildings often says more than its slogans.
abstract.cn: 一个社会怎样对待最老的建筑，往往比它的口号更能说明问题。

abstract.en: Between a hint and a proof there is one step, and this phrase deliberately stays on the first side.
abstract.cn: 提示与证明之间隔着一步，这个短语有意留在前一边。

examples.en: A sudden drop in attendance can be indicative of a deeper problem with the timetable.
examples.cn: 出勤率突然下降可能表明课程表存在更深的问题。

examples.en: Fossil shells in this layer can be indicative of a shallow sea that once covered the plain.
examples.cn: 这一层里的贝壳化石可能表明这片平原过去曾是浅海。

examples.en: Her choice of words can be indicative of how much she distrusts the plan.
examples.cn: 她的用词可能表明她对这项计划有多不信任。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「比 因迪凯提夫 奥夫」——手指一指，只指方向不下结论：表明；预示

root: 拉丁语 indicare「指出」（in-「向内」+ dicare「宣告」）→ 形容词 indicativus；短语本身是英语「be + 形容词 + of」框架，属现代搭配，首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a bare sign to a hedged inference: existence, forecast, data, clinical hint, ancient trace, academic caution, symbolic marking and a clue that stops short of proof.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从单纯的迹象走到留有余地的推断：存在、预示、数据、临床提示、远古痕迹、学术措辞、象征标记，以及止步于线索而非证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circled number on a lab sheet points at an infection without naming it.
core.cn: 核心意象：化验单上一个被圈出的数值，指向感染却不点破。

branches.en: THE POINTER: a visible sign points at something present but unseen.
branches.cn: 指向：可见的迹象指出存在却看不见的东西。

branches.en: THE FORECAST: the same gesture turns toward what has not happened yet.
branches.cn: 预示：同一个手势转向尚未发生的事。

branches.en: THE PATTERN AND THE BODY: figures mark a trend, and a clinic reads them as illness.
branches.cn: 规律与身体：数字标出趋势，诊室把它们读成疾病。

branches.en: THE RELIC AND THE HEDGE: remains point at a lost world, and scholars keep the claim soft.
branches.cn: 遗迹与余地：遗存指向消失的世界，学者把话说得留有余地。

branches.en: THE SYMBOL AND THE LIMIT: habits can mark values, and a sign is still not a proof.
branches.cn: 象征与限度：习惯可以标出价值，而迹象仍不等于证明。

intro.en: The family rests on one Latin verb of proclaiming, with prefixes and endings doing the grammatical work.
intro.cn: 整个词族靠一个表示「宣告」的拉丁动词立住，语法变化由前缀与词尾承担。

latinIntro.en: Latin dicare and indicare supply the core; in- and the endings -ive, -ation and -or build the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dicare 与 indicare 提供核心，in- 与 -ive、-ation、-or 等词尾构成其余部分。

items.example: It is the older verb behind the family of pointing words.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一族「指出」类词背后更古老的动词。

items.example: It turns dicare into a verb of pointing at something.
items.exampleCN: 它把 dicare 变成指向某物的动词。

items.example: It is the direct source of indicate.
items.exampleCN: 它是指出这个词的直接来源。

items.example: It turns the verb stem into indicativus and then indicative.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词干变成 indicativus，再成为 indicative。

items.example: It named the mood of plain statement in grammar.
items.exampleCN: 它在语法里为陈述语气命名。

items.example: It forms indication from indicate.
items.exampleCN: 它由 indicate 构成 indication。

items.example: It forms indicator, the thing that points.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 indicator，即用来指示的东西。

items.example: It belongs to the same pointing family and later meant a list.
items.exampleCN: 它同属「指出」一族，后来指索引。

items.example: It forms indicatively from the adjective.

由动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「指标」

definition_zh: adj. 可食用的；能入口的 n. 食品；可食之物
definition_en: safe and suitable to be eaten; good enough to be eaten though not necessarily pleasant; an item of food

dict_mnemonic.text: edible ＝ ed-（吃，拉丁语 edere）＋ -ible（能够被…的）＝「能够被吃的」。同一词根 edere 还给出 edacious（贪吃的）、comestible（可食的；食品），反义加 in- 得 inedible（不能吃的），名词 edibility（可食性）。注意 edible 有两层：一是「无毒、吃得安全」，用于蘑菇、野菜、昆虫；二是「口感上吃得下去」，barely edible 就是「勉强能吃」。复数 edibles 作名词指「食品」。近义 eatable 更口语，palatable 强调「可口」，comestible 偏正式。别把 edible（能吃）与 audible（能听）搞混，两者只是共用 -ible 这个「能够被…」的后缀。

root: 拉丁语 edere（吃）＋ -bilis（能够被…）→ edibilis（可吃的）→ edible（可食用的；食品）

definition_zh: 矿化；成矿作用；（水的）矿化度
definition_en: the process by which organic matter is converted into mineral form, or by which minerals are deposited in rock or tissue
core_image: 一根骨头埋进岩层，逐渐被矿物替换，旁边是一条发亮的矿脉
scene: 这里指「矿化」。 The fossil's bone had undergone complete mineralization, so no original tissue remained.
sceneCN: 这里 mineralization 指「矿化取代」（第 1 个义项：有机组织被矿物逐步替换的过程）；骨组织已被矿物完全取代，原有组织不再存在。图中可辨识物件：化石骨、岩层剖面、矿物沉积、放大镜。

pos.zh: 矿化；成矿作用；矿化度（多作不可数名词）

senses.title: Replacement by minerals
senses.titleCN: 矿化取代：有机组织被矿物替换
senses.definition: the process by which minerals replace organic tissue, as in the fossilisation of bone or wood
senses.definitionCN: 矿物替换有机组织的过程，如骨骼或木材的化石化的过程
senses.example: The wood's cell walls survived only as mineralization.
senses.exampleCN: 木头的细胞壁只以矿化形态保存下来。
senses.why: Because ground water slowly deposits minerals in the spaces of tissue, the process is named after what fills the space.
senses.whyCN: 由于地下水缓慢地把矿物沉积在组织的空隙里，这个过程便以填入空隙的东西命名。

senses.title: Release of soil nutrients
senses.titleCN: 土壤矿化：有机养分转为可吸收的离子
senses.definition: in soil science, the conversion of organic nitrogen and phosphorus into inorganic ions that plants can take up
senses.definitionCN: 土壤科学中指把有机氮、有机磷转化为植物可吸收的无机离子
senses.example: Warm, moist soil speeds up nitrogen mineralization.
senses.exampleCN: 温暖潮湿的土壤会加快氮的矿化。
senses.why: Here the direction is the reverse of fossilisation: organic matter breaks down into mineral ions instead of being replaced by them.
senses.whyCN: 这里的方向与化石化的方向相反：有机质分解成矿物离子，而不是被矿物替换。

senses.title: Ore formation
senses.titleCN: 成矿作用：金属富集进岩脉
senses.definition: in economic geology, the concentration of ore minerals into a deposit by hydrothermal or magmatic processes
senses.definitionCN: 经济地质学中指经热液或岩浆过程把矿石矿物富集成矿床
senses.example: The gold mineralization follows a quartz vein for several kilometres.
senses.exampleCN: 金的成矿作用沿一条石英脉延伸数公里。
senses.why: Geologists borrow the general 'becoming mineral' word for the specific event that makes a deposit worth mining.
senses.whyCN: 地质学家借用「变成矿物」这一泛称，专指使矿床值得开采的那个事件。

senses.title: Tissue calcification
senses.titleCN: 组织钙化：医学上的矿物沉积
senses.definition: in medicine, the abnormal deposition of calcium minerals in soft tissue such as arteries or kidneys
senses.definitionCN: 医学中指钙矿物异常沉积在动脉、肾脏等软组织里
senses.example: Arterial mineralization stiffens the vessel wall.
senses.exampleCN: 动脉矿化使血管壁变硬。
senses.why: Clinical writing uses the same word as geology because the deposit is chemically the same kind of mineral.
senses.whyCN: 临床写作与地质学使用同一个词，因为沉积物在化学上是同一类矿物。

senses.title: Biomineralization
senses.titleCN: 生物矿化：生物主动构建矿物
senses.definition: the controlled formation of minerals by living organisms, as in shells, teeth and bone
senses.definitionCN: 生物受控地形成矿物，如贝壳、牙齿与骨骼
senses.example: Coral biomineralization builds reefs from dissolved carbonate.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚的生物矿化用溶解的碳酸盐造礁。
senses.why: Biologists add the prefix bio- to separate deliberate construction by cells from passive geological deposition.
senses.whyCN: 生物学家加前缀 bio-，把细胞有意的建造与被动的地址沉积区分开。

senses.title: Mineral content of water
senses.titleCN: 矿化度：水中溶解矿物的总量
senses.definition: in hydrology, the total dissolved mineral content of water, also called its degree of mineralization
senses.definitionCN: 水文学中指水中溶解矿物的总量，也称矿化度
senses.example: The well's high mineralization makes the water unsuitable for irrigation.
senses.exampleCN: 这口井矿化度高，水不适合灌溉。
senses.why: The process word doubles as a quantity, because the result of dissolved minerals accumulating is a measurable total.
senses.whyCN: 过程词兼作数量词，因为矿物溶解累积的结果就是一个可测量的总量。

senses.title: Complete breakdown of pollutants
senses.titleCN: 污染物彻底矿化：分解为无机终产物
senses.definition: in environmental chemistry, the complete conversion of an organic pollutant into carbon dioxide, water and inorganic salts
senses.definitionCN: 环境化学中指把有机污染物完全转化为二氧化碳、水与无机盐
senses.example: The treatment aims for full mineralization of the solvent.
senses.exampleCN: 该处理的目标是让溶剂彻底矿化。
senses.why: Regulators care whether a pollutant is destroyed or merely transformed, so 'complete mineralization' became a standard.
senses.whyCN: 监管者关心污染物是被销毁还是仅仅被转化，因此「彻底矿化」成了标准说法。

senses.title: Preservation in archaeology
senses.titleCN: 考古保存：矿化留下的遗存
senses.definition: in archaeology, the mineral replacement that lets bone, shell or metal survive in the ground for millennia
senses.definitionCN: 考古学中指矿物替换使骨骼、贝壳或金属得以在地下保存数千年
senses.example: Only the mineralized parts of the burial survived the wet soil.
senses.exampleCN: 只有墓葬中已矿化的部分在湿土中保存下来。
senses.why: Archaeologists rely on the same process to explain why some objects last and others vanish.
senses.whyCN: 考古学家依靠同一过程来解释为何有些物件留存、有些消失。

intro.en: Mineralization joins mineral, from Medieval Latin minera 'ore', to the verb suffix -ize and the action ending -ation.
intro.cn: mineralization 把源自中世纪拉丁 minera「矿石」的 mineral，与动词后缀 -ize 和动作词尾 -ation 组合起来。

items.en: Minera meant 'ore, mine' in medieval mining texts. Its deeper origin is disputed, with a Celtic ore word as the usual hypothesis.
items.cn: minera 在中世纪采矿文献中意为「矿石、矿」。其更深来源有争议，通常的假说是某个凯尔特语表示矿石的词。

items.en: The verb suffix -ize came into English through French -iser, which itself rests on Greek -izein 'to do, to make'.
items.cn: 动词后缀 -ize 经法语 -iser 进入英语，而法语形式又建立在希腊 -izein「做、使」之上。

items.en: The action ending -ation descends from Latin -atio, so the whole word reads as 'the making of mineral'.
items.cn: 动作词尾 -ation 出自拉丁 -atio，因此整个词读作「使成为矿物的过程」。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geology applied the word to ore deposition and to the replacement of organic matter in fossils.
items.cn: 19 世纪地质学把这个词用于成矿作用，也用于化石中有机物被替换的过程。

items.en: Twentieth-century soil science and hydrology extended it to nutrient release and to the dissolved mineral load of water.
items.cn: 20 世纪的土壤学与水文学又把它扩展到养分释放与水中溶解矿物总量。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the first English use of mineralization is uncertain, and the deeper origin of minera is unresolved; the Celtic link is a hypothesis rather than a recorded fact.
items.cn: 来源不确定：mineralization 的英语首见年代存疑，minera 的更深来源亦无定论；凯尔特语关联属假说而非有记录的事实。

note.en: The first group holds mineral-family words that name different things; the second holds processes that also preserve or harden tissue.
note.cn: 第一组是同属 mineral 词族但指不同事物的词；第二组是同样保存或硬化组织的其他过程。

entries.definition: The science of minerals. Mineralization is a process; mineralogy is the discipline that studies its products.
entries.definitionCN: 研究矿物的学科。mineralization 是过程，mineralogy 是研究其产物的学科。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to convert into mineral form. Mineralization is its noun, naming the same event as a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 意为使转化为矿物形态的动词。mineralization 是其名词，把同一事件当作事物来命名。

entries.definition: The natural inorganic solid itself. Mineralization names the process by which such material forms or replaces something.
entries.definitionCN: 天然无机固体本身。mineralization 命名这种材料形成或替换某物的过程。

entries.definition: The whole process of turning a living thing into a fossil. Mineralization is often the mechanism, but freezing or drying can also preserve.
entries.definitionCN: 把生物变成化石的整个过程。矿化常是其中的机制，但冷冻或干燥也能保存。

entries.definition: The deposition of calcium salts in tissue. Mineralization in medicine often means calcification, but it can involve other minerals.
entries.definitionCN: 钙盐在组织中的沉积。医学中的矿化常指钙化，但也可能涉及其他矿物。

entries.definition: The physical and chemical changes that turn loose sediment into rock. Mineralization is one of the changes it includes.
entries.definitionCN: 把松散沉积物变成岩石的物理与化学变化。矿化是其中包含的一种变化。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: mineral + -ize + -ation: the process of becoming mineral.
normal.cn: mineral + -ize + -ation：变成矿物的过程。

normal.en: The family runs mineralize, mineralized, mineral, mineralogy and demineralization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mineralize、mineralized、mineral、mineralogy、demineralization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: soil mineralization, ore mineralization, degree of mineralization.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：土壤矿化、成矿作用、矿化度。

normal.en: In soil, mineralization releases nutrients; in fossils, it replaces tissue; the word covers both directions.
normal.cn: 在土壤中矿化释放养分，在化石中矿化替换组织；这个词覆盖了两个方向。

normal.en: Biomineralization is mineralization run by cells, as in shells and teeth.
normal.cn: 生物矿化是由细胞执行的矿化，如贝壳与牙齿。

abstract.en: Picture a bone in wet ground slowly filling with stone until none of it is bone.
abstract.cn: 想象湿土中的骨头慢慢被石头填满，直到一点也不剩骨。

abstract.en: Picture a dark vein threading through grey rock, marking where metal was concentrated.
abstract.cn: 想象一条暗色矿脉穿过灰色岩石，标出金属富集之处。

abstract.en: Picture a glass of well water leaving a white ring when it evaporates.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯井水蒸发后留下一圈白痕。

examples.en: Warm weather increased the mineralization of soil organic matter.
examples.cn: 温暖天气提高了土壤有机质的矿化速度。

examples.en: The degree of mineralization determines whether the water is drinkable.
examples.cn: 矿化度决定这水能否饮用。

examples.en: The company claims complete mineralization of the pesticide within a week.
examples.cn: 该公司声称这种农药在一周内可彻底矿化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mineral（矿物）+ ization（化）」——变成矿物的过程 → mineralization 矿化

root: 中世纪拉丁 minera「矿石」→ mineral；加希腊 -izein 与拉丁 -atio → mineralization。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one process in both directions: minerals replacing tissue, organic matter releasing ions, ores concentrating, arteries hardening, cells building shells, water carrying salts, pollutants dissolving and graves preserving bone.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一过程向两个方向展开：矿物替换组织、有机质释放离子、矿石富集、动脉硬化、细胞造壳、水携带盐、污染物被分解、墓葬保存骨骼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bone turning to stone inside a layer of rock.
core.cn: 核心意象：岩层中的骨头变成石头。

branches.en: REPLACEMENT: fossils and burials survive because minerals take the place of tissue.
branches.cn: 替换：化石与墓葬之所以留存，是因为矿物取代了组织。

branches.en: RELEASE: in soil, the same word runs the other way and turns organic matter into ions.
branches.cn: 释放：在土壤中，同一个词反向运行，把有机质变成离子。

branches.en: CONCENTRATION: economic geology names the event that makes a deposit worth mining.
branches.cn: 富集：经济地质学以此命名使矿床值得开采的事件。

branches.en: BODY: cells can build mineral deliberately, or deposit it where it does not belong.
branches.cn: 身体：细胞可以有意构建矿物，也可以把它沉积在不该在的地方。

branches.en: MEASURE AND REMEDY: water reports mineralization as a number, and treatment aims for its completion.
branches.cn: 计量与治理：水以数字报告矿化度，处理则以彻底矿化为目标。

intro.en: Mineralization combines a Medieval Latin noun, a Greek-derived verb suffix and a Latin action ending, three layers from three languages.
intro.cn: mineralization 把一个中世纪拉丁名词、一个源自希腊的动词后缀与一个拉丁动作词尾合在一起，三层来自三种语言。

latinIntro.en: Latin -atio gave the noun ending; the -ize layer came through French from Greek -izein; and minera supplied the stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 -atio 提供名词词尾，-ize 一层经法语来自希腊 -izein，minera 提供词干。

items.meaning: the process of becoming or replacing with mineral
items.meaningCN: 变成矿物或用矿物替换的过程
items.example: Mineralization preserved the shell.
Bacteria mineralize the leaf litter.
The mineralized tissue is hard as stone.
The mineral is mostly calcium phosphate.
Demineralization weakens the enamel.

items.meaning: a substance or fluid that promotes mineralization
items.meaningCN: 促进矿化的物质或流体
items.example: The mineralizer carried dissolved silica.
items.exampleCN: 该矿化剂携带溶解的二氧化硅。

items.meaningCN: 由生物控制的矿物形成
items.example: Biomineralization builds coral reefs.
Mineralogy explains the crystal shapes.
items.exampleCN: 矿物学解释了晶体的形状。

items.meaning: the wider process of becoming a fossil
items.example: Fossilization required rapid burial.

definition_zh: 指数的；指数式的；以指数函数表示的；急剧增长的
definition_en: relating to an exponent or an exponential function, or describing a rate of change that keeps multiplying by a fixed factor
core_image: 一条曲线在右端几乎竖直上冲，越走越陡
scene: 一张曲线图上，细线过了某一天后几乎竖直上冲。 The curve shows exponential growth after the first week of the outbreak.
sceneCN: 这里 exponential 指「按指数规律增长，即每过一段就乘上同一个倍数」（第 3 个义项：指数式增长）；句意为疫情第一周之后，曲线呈现指数增长。图中可辨识物件：坐标轴、向上弯的曲线、标尺、图钉。

pos.zh: 指数的；指数式的；急剧增长的
指数函数（数学中作名词用）

senses.title: Relating to an exponent
senses.definition: connected with an exponent, the raised number that shows a power
senses.definitionCN: 与幂指数那个抬高的数有关的
senses.example: The exponential notation places the power above the base.
senses.exampleCN: 指数记法把幂写底数上方。
senses.why: the adjective simply says 'of an exponent', and the base word is the Latin participle for setting something out.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只说「属于指数的」，而它的基词正是那个表示「摆出来」的拉丁分词。

senses.title: Having a variable in the exponent
senses.definition: describing an expression in which the variable appears in the exponent rather than the base
senses.definitionCN: 描述变量出现在指数位置而不是底数位置的表达式
senses.example: An exponential equation cannot be solved by simple factoring.
senses.exampleCN: 指数方程不能靠简单的因式分解来解。
senses.why: what makes such an equation exponential is precisely that the unknown has climbed into the exponent.
senses.whyCN: 这类方程之所以称为指数的，正因为未知数爬到了指数位置上。

senses.title: The exponential function
senses.definition: a function in which a fixed base is raised to a variable power
senses.definitionCN: 以固定底数取变量次幂的函数
senses.example: The exponential describes growth proportional to the current amount.
senses.exampleCN: 指数函数描述与当前数量成正比的增长。
senses.why: the function is named by the piece that varies, the exponent, rather than by the fixed base.
senses.whyCN: 这个函数以变化的那一部分命名，也就是指数，而不是固定的底数。

senses.title: Exponential growth
senses.definition: growth in which the amount keeps being multiplied by the same factor
senses.definitionCN: 每次都用同一个倍数乘上去的增长
senses.example: Bacteria in a warm dish show exponential growth at first.
senses.exampleCN: 温盘里的细菌起初呈指数增长。
senses.why: when each step multiplies by a constant factor, the exponent rises steadily, so the word for the exponent names the pattern.
senses.whyCN: 当每一步都乘上同一个常数倍数时，指数稳步上升，于是指数的名字成了这种模式的名字。

senses.title: Exponential decay
senses.definition: a fall in which the amount keeps being divided by the same factor
senses.definitionCN: 每次都被同一个倍数除下去、不断减少的过程
senses.example: The radioactivity of the sample follows exponential decay.
senses.exampleCN: 样品的放射性遵循指数衰减。
senses.why: decay mirrors growth: the exponent goes down at a steady rate, so the same adjective covers both directions.
senses.whyCN: 衰减是增长的镜像：指数按稳定速率下降，因此同一个形容词覆盖两个方向。

senses.title: The exponential distribution
senses.definition: a probability distribution that describes the waiting time between events occurring at a constant rate
senses.definitionCN: 描述以恒定速率发生的事件之间等待时间的概率分布
senses.example: The waiting times at the call centre fit an exponential distribution.
senses.exampleCN: 呼叫中心的等待时间符合指数分布。
senses.why: the distribution's curve falls away like an exponential decay, so statistics borrowed the adjective for it.
senses.whyCN: 这条分布的曲线像指数衰减一样往下掉，统计因此借用了这个形容词。

senses.title: Exponential smoothing
senses.definition: a forecasting method that gives recent observations exponentially greater weight
senses.definitionCN: 给近期观测值按指数递减的权重、用来预测的方法
senses.example: Exponential smoothing tracks the sales trend without chasing every spike.
senses.exampleCN: 指数平滑能跟踪销售趋势，又不去追每一个尖峰。
senses.why: the weights fall off in an exponential pattern, so the method is named after the shape of its weighting.
senses.whyCN: 权重按指数形态递减，这个方法便以其权重的形状命名。

senses.title: Exponential running time
senses.definition: describing an algorithm whose running time grows exponentially with the size of its input
senses.definitionCN: 描述运行时间随输入规模按指数增长的算法
senses.example: The brute-force search runs in exponential time on large inputs.
senses.exampleCN: 这种穷举搜索在大输入上以指数时间运行。
senses.why: computer science counts steps; when the count doubles with each added item, the growth is exponential.
senses.whyCN: 计算机科学数的是步数；每多一个数据步数就翻倍，这种增长就是指数的。

senses.title: The exponential as a noun
senses.definition: the exponential function itself, used as a noun in mathematics
senses.definitionCN: 数学中直接作名词用的指数函数
senses.example: The exponential turns addition into multiplication.
senses.exampleCN: 指数函数把加法变成乘法。
senses.why: mathematicians routinely drop the word function and let the adjective stand alone as a noun.
senses.whyCN: 数学家习惯省掉「函数」二字，让这个形容词直接当名词用。

intro.en: Exponential is English exponent plus the adjective suffix -al. The base goes back to Latin exponere 'to set forth', and the mathematical use dates from the age of calculus.
intro.cn: exponential 是英语 exponent 加形容词后缀 -al 构成。其基词上溯到拉丁 exponere「摆出来」，数学用法则始于微积分时代。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus ponere 'to put' gave exponere 'to set out, explain'; the participle exponens became English exponent.
items.cn: ex-「出」加 ponere「放」构成 exponere「摆出来、解释」；分词 exponens 成为英语 exponent。

items.en: Exponent entered English as a noun for an explainer, and only later acquired the mathematical sense of a raised power.
items.cn: exponent 最初以「解释者」的名词身份进入英语，后来才获得「幂指数」的数学义。

items.en: The Latin adjective ending -alis, through French -al, turns a noun into an adjective of relation; exponent plus -al gives exponential.
items.cn: 拉丁形容词词尾 -alis 经法语 -al，把名词变成表示关系的形容词；exponent 加 -al 得 exponential。

items.en: From the late seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the adjective named functions and equations in which the variable sits in the exponent.
items.cn: 从十七世纪末到十八世纪，这个形容词用来指变量位于指数位置的函数与方程。

items.en: During the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the word spread to decay, probability distributions, forecasting and computing, always naming growth or fall by a constant factor.
items.cn: 在十九、二十世纪，这个词扩展到衰变、概率分布、预测与计算，始终指按固定倍数增长或下降。

items.en: The exact first date for each applied sense is approximate; the morphological pieces are fully attested.
items.cn: 每个应用义的确切首见年代都是约数；构词的两个部分则有充分记录。

note.en: The first group shares the exponent stem and is easily misread; the second group names other ways of describing rapid or steady change.
note.cn: 第一组共享 exponent 这个词干，容易被误读；第二组是描述快速或稳定变化的其他说法。

entries.definition: The raised number itself or an advocate; the adjective exponential adds the sense of a pattern of change.
entries.definitionCN: 指那个抬高的数，或指倡导者；形容词 exponential 则加上「变化模式」的意思。

entries.definition: The operation of raising to a power, not the shape of a growth curve.
entries.definitionCN: 指求幂这个运算，而非增长曲线的形状。

entries.definition: From expandere 'to spread out', built on pandere, not ponere: it means wide or open, not growing by a factor.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 expandere「铺开」，词根是 pandere 而非 ponere：意为宽广、开阔，不是按倍数增长。

entries.definition: From expendere 'to weigh out, pay', built on pendere: it means costly, not fast-growing.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 expendere「称出、支付」，词根是 pendere：意为昂贵，不是快速增长。

entries.definition: A rare word meaning able to be explained, from the same exponere; it has nothing to do with growth.
entries.definitionCN: 罕见词，意为「可解释的」，同出 exponere；与增长无关。

entries.definition: Simply fast; it says nothing about the rule by which the amount increases.
entries.definitionCN: 只表示快，不说明数量按什么规则增加。

entries.definition: Describes a sudden burst of growth; exponential describes a steady multiplication that eventually looks like a burst.
entries.definitionCN: 描述突然爆发的增长；exponential 描述一种稳定的倍数增长，最终看起来像爆发。

entries.definition: In growth language, geometric increase also multiplies by a fixed factor; the two terms often coincide, though geometric is the older label.
entries.definitionCN: 在增长语境里，几何增长同样按固定倍数相乘；两个说法常常重合，只是几何一词更老。

entries.definition: Speeding up in general; exponential growth is one specific rule that produces acceleration.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指越来越快；指数增长是产生加速度的一种具体规则。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Exponent plus -al: the adjective of the raised number, then the name of the curve it produces.
normal.cn: exponent 加 -al：先是指数这个数的形容词，再成为它所画出的曲线的名字。

normal.en: The family runs exponent, exponential, exponentially, exponentiation and exponentiate.
normal.cn: 同族词有 exponent、exponential、exponentially、exponentiation 与 exponentiate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the applications: exponential growth, exponential decay, exponential distribution.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出应用场景：指数增长、指数衰减、指数分布。

normal.en: Exponential growth doubles, then doubles again; each doubling is short Scotch tape on the same stack.
normal.cn: 指数增长翻一倍，再翻一倍；每次翻倍都是往同一摞上再贴一层。

normal.en: Exponential decay is the same tape being peeled off at a steady fraction each step.
normal.cn: 指数衰减则是每一步都按固定比例撕掉一层同样的胶带。

abstract.en: Picture a curve that looks lazy for a long time, then suddenly stands up on its tail.
abstract.cn: 想象一条曲线长期懒洋洋地躺着，然后突然用尾巴立起来。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour that doubles its listeners every hour, until the room cannot hold them.
abstract.cn: 想象一个传闻每过一小时听众人数就翻倍，直到房间装不下。

abstract.en: Picture a cup of coffee cooling by the same fraction every minute, never quite reaching room temperature.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯咖啡每分钟按同一比例降温，永远差一点才到室温。

examples.en: The number of cases showed exponential growth before the restrictions began.
examples.cn: 限制措施开始前，病例数呈指数增长。

examples.en: The exponential decay of the signal made the far stations inaudible.
examples.cn: 信号的指数衰减让远处的台听不见了。

examples.en: That algorithm is exponential, so it is useless once the list gets long.
examples.cn: 那个算法是指数级的，列表一长就没用了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「往外放」的叠法——一层层往外翻上去 → 指数式的、急剧增长

root: 英语 exponent（指数，源自拉丁 exponens「摆出来的」）+ 形容词后缀 -al。拉丁词根为 exponere = ex-（出）+ ponere（放）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one shape: a number placed above a base, then the function built from it, then the curve that doubles or halves by a fixed factor, and finally the places where that curve appears in data and machines.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项顺着同一个形状展开：一个数被放到基座上方，然后是由它构成的函数，再是那个按固定倍数翻倍或减半的曲线，最后是这条曲线在数据与机器里出现的地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curve that looks almost flat and then stands up on its tail.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条起初几乎是平的，后来用尾巴立起来的曲线。

branches.en: THE RAISED NUMBER: the adjective belongs to the exponent, and to equations where the unknown sits there.
branches.cn: 抬高的数：这个形容词属于指数，也属于未知数坐在指数位置的方程。

branches.en: THE FUNCTION: the exponential function, whether named in full or shortened to a bare noun.
branches.cn: 函数本身：无论说全称还是缩成一个光秃秃的名词，指的都是指数函数。

branches.en: UP AND DOWN: growth and decay are the same fixed-factor rule running forward or backward.
branches.cn: 上升与下降：增长与衰减是同一条固定倍数规则的正向与反向。

branches.en: MEASURING TIME: waiting times and smoothed forecasts borrow the shape of the decay curve.
branches.cn: 计量时间：等待时间与平滑预测都借用了衰减曲线的形状。

branches.en: TIME THAT EXPLODES: in computing the step count doubles with every added item.
branches.cn: 爆炸的时间：在计算里，每多一个数据，步数就翻倍。

intro.en: Exponential is an English noun plus a Latin adjective suffix, and both parts are still productive.
intro.cn: exponential 是一个英语名词加拉丁形容词后缀构成，两部分至今都能产。

latinIntro.en: The base exponere also gives exponent, expound and expose; the suffix -alis, through French -al, builds adjectives of relation.
latinIntro.cn: 基词 exponere 还衍生 exponent、expound 与 expose；后缀 -alis 经法语 -al 构成表示关系的形容词。

items.example: The prefix puts the number out of the base's body.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把这个数放到基座之外。

items.example: The base verb supplies the placing.
items.exampleCN: 基词提供「放置」这个动作。

items.example: The participle became the noun exponent.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词成了名词 exponent。

items.example: The exponent rides above the base.
The adjective names the curve as well as the number.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词既指数，也指曲线。

items.example: Costs grew exponentially.

items.meaning: the act of raising to a power
items.example: Exponentiation repeats multiplication.
The program exponentiated the matrix.

items.meaningCN: 表示关系的形容词后缀
items.example: It turns a noun into an adjective of belonging.
items.exampleCN: 它把名词变成表示归属的形容词。
